sentences.zh: 【後晉紀四】　起玄默攝提格，盡閼逢執徐正月，凡二年有奇。

translations.literal: [Later Jin Annals 4] From Xuanni Shetige through Efeng Zhixu, first month; a little more than two years in all.
translations.idiomatic: [Later Jin Annals 4] From Xuanni Shetige through Efeng Zhixu, first month—two years and a fraction in all.

sentences.zh: 高祖聖文章武明德孝皇帝下天福七年（

translations.literal: Below the Sacred Literary Martial Virtuous Filial Emperor Gaozu, Tianfu year 7 (
translations.idiomatic: Reign of the Sacred Literary Martial Virtuous Filial Emperor Gaozu, Tianfu year 7 (

sentences.zh: 壬寅，公元九四二年）

translations.literal: renyin, 942 CE)
translations.idiomatic: renyin, 942 CE)

sentences.zh: 春，正月，丁巳，鎮州牙將自西郭水碾門導官軍入城，殺守陴民二萬人，執安重榮，斬之。

translations.literal: In spring, the first month, on dingsi, a Zhenzhou yaji led the government army into the city through the Xiguo watermill gate, killed twenty thousand common people defending the wall, seized An Chongrong, and beheaded him.
translations.idiomatic: In spring, the first month, on dingsi, a Zhenzhou garrison officer led government troops into the city through the West Suburb watermill gate, slaughtered twenty thousand civilians defending the walls, seized An Chongrong, and executed him.

sentences.zh: 杜重威殺導者，自以為功。

translations.literal: Du Chongwei killed the guide and claimed the credit for himself.
translations.idiomatic: Du Chongwei killed the guide and took credit for the victory himself.

sentences.zh: 庚申，重榮首至鄴都，帝命漆之，函送契丹。

translations.literal: On gengshen, Chongrong's head arrived at Yedu; the emperor ordered it lacquered and sent in a box to the Khitan.
translations.idiomatic: On gengshen, Chongrong's head reached the capital at Yedu. The emperor had it lacquered and dispatched in a casket to the Khitan.

sentences.zh: 癸亥，改鎮州為恆州，成德軍為順國軍。

translations.literal: On guihai, Zhenzhou was changed to Hengzhou, and the Chengde army became the Shunguo army.
translations.idiomatic: On guihai, the court renamed Zhenzhou Hengzhou and redesignated the Chengde army as the Shunguo army.

sentences.zh: 丙寅，以門下侍郎、同平章事趙瑩為侍中，以杜重威為順國節度使兼侍中。

translations.literal: On bingyin, Zhao Ying, vice director of the Secretariat and co-administrator of the Secretariat-Chancellery, was made chief minister of the Palace Secretariat, and Du Chongwei was made military governor of Shunguo and chief minister of the Palace Secretariat concurrently.
translations.idiomatic: On bingyin, Zhao Ying, vice director of the Secretariat and co-administrator of the Secretariat-Chancellery, was promoted to chief minister of the Palace Secretariat, while Du Chongwei was appointed military governor of Shunguo with concurrent status as chief minister of the Palace Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 安重榮私財及恆州府庫，重威盡有之，帝知而不問。

translations.literal: An Chongrong's private wealth and the Hengzhou treasury—Du Chongwei took them all; the emperor knew but did not inquire.
translations.idiomatic: Du Chongwei seized all of An Chongrong's private property together with the Hengzhou treasury, and though the emperor knew of it, he made no inquiry.

sentences.zh: 又表衛尉少卿范陽王瑜為副使，瑜為之重斂於民，恆人不勝其苦。

translations.literal: He also memorialized the vice director of the Court of Imperial Regalia, Wang Yu of Fanyang, as deputy commissioner; Yu on his behalf heavily levied the people, and the people of Heng could not bear the suffering.
translations.idiomatic: Du Chongwei also recommended Wang Yu of Fanyang, vice director of the Court of Imperial Regalia, as his deputy commissioner. Yu imposed heavy exactions on the people on Du's behalf, until the populace of Heng could endure no more.

sentences.zh: 張式父鐸詣闕訟冤。

translations.literal: Zhang Shi's father Duo went to the palace to lodge a grievance over injustice.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Du, father of Zhang Shi, traveled to the capital to protest the injustice done to his son.

sentences.zh: 壬午，以河陽節度使王周為彰義節度使，代張彥澤。

translations.literal: On renwu, Wang Zhou, military governor of Heyang, was made military governor of Zhangyi, replacing Zhang Yanze.
translations.idiomatic: On renwu, Wang Zhou, military governor of Heyang, was appointed military governor of Zhangyi in Zhang Yanze's stead.

sentences.zh: 閩主曦立皇后李氏，同平章事真之女也；

translations.literal: The Min ruler Xi installed Li as empress; she was the daughter of co-administrator Zhen.
translations.idiomatic: The Min ruler Xi installed Lady Li as empress—she was the daughter of co-administrator Zhen.

sentences.zh: 嗜酒剛愎，曦寵而憚之。

translations.literal: She loved wine and was obstinate; Xi favored her yet feared her.
translations.idiomatic: Given to drink and willful by nature, she was both favored and feared by Xi.

sentences.zh: 彰武節度使丁審琪，養部曲千人，縱之為暴於境內；

translations.literal: Ding Shenqi, military governor of Zhangwu, maintained a thousand retainers and let them run wild committing violence within his jurisdiction;
translations.idiomatic: Zhangwu military governor Ding Shenqi maintained a private force of a thousand retainers and turned them loose to terrorize the countryside within his jurisdiction;

sentences.zh: 軍校賀行政與諸胡相結為亂，攻延州，帝遣曹州防禦使何重建將兵救之，同、鄜援兵繼至，乃得免。

translations.literal: The army officer He Xingzheng joined with various Hu in rebellion, attacked Yanzhou; the emperor dispatched Caozhou defense commissioner He Chongjian to lead troops to rescue it; reinforcements from Tong and Fu successively arrived, and the city was saved.
translations.idiomatic: Army officer He Xingzheng allied with various non-Han groups in rebellion and attacked Yanzhou. The emperor sent Caozhou defense commissioner He Chongjian with troops to the relief of the city. Reinforcements from Tong and Fu arrived in succession, and Yanzhou was spared.

sentences.zh: 二月，癸已，以重建為彰武留後，召審琪歸朝。

translations.literal: In the second month, on guisi, He Chongjian was made acting governor of Zhangwu, and Ding Shenqi was recalled to court.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month, on guisi, He Chongjian was appointed acting governor of Zhangwu, and Ding Shenqi was recalled to the capital.

sentences.zh: 重建，雲、朔間胡人也。

translations.literal: Chongjian was a Hu man from the region of Yun and Shuo.
translations.idiomatic: He Chongjian was a non-Han native of the Yun-Shuo frontier.

sentences.zh: 唐左丞相宋齊丘固求豫政事，唐主聽入中書；

translations.literal: Tang Left Grand Counselor Song Qiqiu obstinately sought to participate in government affairs; the Tang ruler allowed him to enter the Central Secretariat;
translations.idiomatic: Tang Left Grand Counselor Song Qiqiu pressed insistently to take part in affairs of state, and the Tang ruler permitted him to enter the Central Secretariat;

sentences.zh: 又求領尚書省，乃罷侍中壽王景遂判尚書省，更領中書、門下省，以齊丘知尚書省事；

translations.literal: He further sought to head the Department of State Affairs, so Prince Jing of Shou, chief minister of the Palace Secretariat who administered the Department of State Affairs, was dismissed from that post and instead put in charge of the Central Secretariat and Chancellery; Song Qiqiu was made director of the Department of State Affairs;
translations.idiomatic: Song Qiqiu then sought to head the Department of State Affairs. Prince Jing of Shou, the chief minister who had been administering that department, was reassigned to oversee the Central Secretariat and Chancellery instead, while Song Qiqiu was placed in charge of the Department of State Affairs;

sentences.zh: 其三省事並取齊王璟參決。

translations.literal: Affairs of all three departments were to be decided with the participation of Prince Qi Jing.
translations.idiomatic: Matters of all three central departments were to be decided with Prince Qi Jing's participation.

sentences.zh: 齊丘視事數月，親吏夏昌圖盜官錢三千緡，齊丘判貸其死；

translations.literal: After Qiqiu took office for several months, a close aide Xia Changtu stole three thousand strings of official money; Qiqiu sentenced him to be forgiven his death penalty;
translations.idiomatic: After several months in office, Qiqiu learned that a trusted subordinate, Xia Changtu, had embezzled three thousand strings of government cash. Qiqiu ruled that his capital crime be commuted;

sentences.zh: 唐主大怒，斬昌圖。

translations.literal: The Tang ruler was greatly angered and beheaded Changtu.
translations.idiomatic: The Tang ruler was furious and had Changtu executed.

sentences.zh: 齊丘稱疾，請罷省事，從之。

translations.literal: Qiqiu claimed illness and requested to be relieved of his post as director; the request was granted.
translations.idiomatic: Qiqiu pleaded illness and asked to be relieved of his duties as department director; the court consented.

sentences.zh: 涇州奏遣押牙陳延暉持敕書詣涼州，州中將吏請延暉為節度使。

translations.literal: Jingzhou reported that it dispatched yaya Chen Yanhui bearing an imperial edict to Liangzhou; the officers and officials of the prefecture requested that Yanhui be made military governor.
translations.idiomatic: Jingzhou reported that it had dispatched envoy Chen Yanhui with an imperial edict to Liangzhou, where the prefecture's officers and officials petitioned to have Yanhui made military governor.

sentences.zh: 三月，閩主曦立長樂王亞澄為閩王。

translations.literal: In the third month, the Min ruler Xi installed Prince of Changle Ya Cheng as Prince of Min.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month, the Min ruler Xi invested Prince of Changle Ya Cheng as Prince of Min.

sentences.zh: 張彥澤在涇州，擅發兵擊諸胡，兵皆敗沒，調民馬千餘匹以補之。

translations.literal: Zhang Yanze, at Jingzhou, on his own authority dispatched troops to attack the various Hu; the troops were all defeated and wiped out; he requisitioned more than a thousand civilian horses to replace them.
translations.idiomatic: While stationed at Jingzhou, Zhang Yanze dispatched troops on his own authority to attack various non-Han groups. His forces were destroyed in defeat, and he requisitioned more than a thousand civilian horses to replenish his losses.

sentences.zh: 還至陝，獲亡將楊洪，乘醉斷其手足而斬之。

translations.literal: Returning to Shan, he captured the deserter general Yang Hong, and while drunk severed his hands and feet and beheaded him.
translations.idiomatic: On his return to Shan, he captured the deserter general Yang Hong, and in a drunken rage severed his hands and feet before executing him.

sentences.zh: 王周奏彥澤在鎮貪殘不法二十六條，民散亡者五千餘戶。

translations.literal: Wang Zhou submitted a memorial listing twenty-six counts of Zhang Yanze's greed, cruelty, and lawlessness while in his command; more than five thousand households of common people had fled.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Zhou memorialized the throne with twenty-six counts of Zhang Yanze's extortion, cruelty, and lawlessness in command. More than five thousand households had fled the region.

sentences.zh: 彥澤既至，帝以其有軍功，又與楊光遠連姻，釋不問。

translations.literal: When Yanze arrived, the emperor, because he had military achievements and was related by marriage to Yang Guangyuan, released him without inquiry.
translations.idiomatic: When Yanze arrived at court, the emperor excused him from investigation on account of his military service and his marriage tie to Yang Guangyuan.

sentences.zh: 夏，四月，己未，右諫議大夫鄭受益上言：「楊洪所以被屠，由陛下去歲送張式與彥澤，使之逞志，致彥澤敢肆凶殘，無所忌憚。

translations.literal: In summer, the fourth month, on jiwei, Right Remonstrance and Editorial Director Zheng Shouyi submitted a memorial: "The reason Yang Hong was slaughtered is that Your Majesty last year sent Zhang Shi to Yanze, allowing him to indulge his will, so that Yanze dares to unleash brutality without fear or restraint.
translations.idiomatic: In summer, the fourth month, on jiwei, Right Remonstrance and Editorial Director Zheng Shouyi memorialized: "Yang Hong was butchered because Your Majesty sent Zhang Shi into Zhang Yanze's hands last year, giving him license to act as he pleased. This emboldened Yanze to commit atrocities without fear or restraint.

sentences.zh: 見聞之人無不切齒，而陛下曾不動心，一無詰讓；

translations.literal: Those who witnessed and heard of it all gnashed their teeth, yet Your Majesty has never stirred at heart or issued a single rebuke;
translations.idiomatic: All who witnessed these deeds grind their teeth in rage, yet Your Majesty has shown neither concern nor reproof—

sentences.zh: 淑慝莫辨，賞罰無章。

translations.literal: good and evil cannot be distinguished; rewards and punishments lack rule.
translations.idiomatic: good cannot be distinguished from evil, and reward and punishment follow no consistent rule.

sentences.zh: 中外皆言陛下受彥澤所獻馬百匹，聽其如是，臣竊為陛下惜此惡名，乞正彥澤罪法，以湔洗聖德。」

translations.literal: Within and without the court all say Your Majesty received one hundred horses presented by Yanze and allowed him to act thus; I privately feel regret for Your Majesty over this evil reputation, and beg that Yanze's crime be judged according to law, to cleanse Your Majesty's sacred virtue."
translations.idiomatic: Court and country alike say Your Majesty accepted a gift of a hundred horses from Yanze and allowed him to go on as he has. I grieve for the stain this casts upon Your Majesty's name and beg that Yanze be punished according to law, so that Your Majesty's sacred virtue may be cleansed."

sentences.zh: 疏奏，留中。

translations.literal: The memorial was submitted and kept within the palace.
translations.idiomatic: The memorial was submitted and withheld within the palace.

sentences.zh: 受益，從讜之兄子也。

translations.literal: Shouyi was the nephew of Congzan's elder brother.
translations.idiomatic: Shouyi was a nephew of Congzan.

sentences.zh: 庚申，刑部郎中李濤等伏閣極論彥澤之罪，語甚切至。

translations.literal: On gengshen, Supervisory Secretary of the Ministry of Justice Li Tao and others knelt at the palace gate and argued strenuously Yanze's crimes; their words were very forceful.
translations.idiomatic: On gengshen, Supervisory Secretary of the Ministry of Justice Li Tao and others kneeled at the palace gate and vehemently denounced Yanze's crimes in the strongest terms.

sentences.zh: 辛酉，敕：「張彥澤削一階，降爵一級。

translations.literal: On xinyou, an edict: "Zhang Yanze is reduced one rank and demoted one noble grade.
translations.idiomatic: On xinyou, an edict was issued: "Zhang Yanze shall be reduced one rank and demoted one grade of nobility.

sentences.zh: 張式父及子弟皆拜官。

translations.literal: Zhang Shi's father and younger brothers are all invested with office.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Shi's father and brothers shall all be granted official appointments.

sentences.zh: 涇州民復業者，減其徭賦。」

translations.literal: For the people of Jingzhou who return to their occupations, their corvée and taxes are reduced."
translations.idiomatic: For the people of Jingzhou who resume their livelihoods, corvée and taxes shall be reduced."

sentences.zh: 癸亥，李濤復與兩省及御史台官伏閣奏彥澤罰太輕，請論如法。

translations.literal: On guihai, Li Tao again together with officials of the two departments and the Censorate knelt at the palace gate and submitted that Yanze's punishment was too light, requesting judgment according to law.
translations.idiomatic: On guihai, Li Tao again kneeled at the palace gate with officials of the two departments and the Censorate to protest that Yanze's punishment was too lenient, petitioning for judgment according to law.

sentences.zh: 帝召濤面諭之。

translations.literal: The emperor summoned Tao and personally instructed him.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor summoned Li Tao and addressed him in person.

sentences.zh: 濤端笏前迫殿陛，論辨聲色俱厲。

translations.literal: Tao held his tablet upright and pressed forward to the palace steps; in debate his voice and expression were both fierce.
translations.idiomatic: Clutching his court tablet, Li Tao pressed forward to the palace steps, arguing with voice and bearing both fierce.

sentences.zh: 帝怒，連叱之，濤不退。

translations.literal: The emperor was angered and repeatedly shouted at him; Tao did not retreat.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor flew into a rage and shouted him down repeatedly, but Li Tao would not withdraw.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「朕已許彥澤不死。」

translations.literal: The emperor said: "I have already promised that Yanze shall not die."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "I have already promised that Yanze shall not die."

sentences.zh: 濤曰：「陛下許彥澤不死，不可負；

translations.literal: Tao said: "Your Majesty's promise that Yanze shall not die cannot be broken;
translations.idiomatic: Li Tao replied, "Your Majesty must keep your promise that Yanze shall not die—

sentences.zh: 不知范延光鐵券安在！」

translations.literal: but where is Fan Yanguang's iron certificate!"
translations.idiomatic: but I wonder where Fan Yanguang's iron certificate of mercy has gone!"

sentences.zh: 帝拂衣起，入禁中。

translations.literal: The emperor swept his robes and rose, entering the inner palace.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor flung aside his robes and stormed into the inner palace.

sentences.zh: 丙寅，以彥澤為左龍武大將軍。

translations.literal: On bingyin, Yanze was made Grand General of the Left Longwu Guard.
translations.idiomatic: On bingyin, Yanze was appointed Grand General of the Left Longwu Guard.

sentences.zh: 漢高祖寢疾，以其子秦王弘度、晉王弘熙皆驕恣，少子越王弘昌孝謹有智識，與右僕射兼西御院使王翷謀出弘度鎮邕州，弘熙鎮容州，而立弘昌。

translations.literal: The Han Gaozu lay ill; because his sons the Prince of Qin Hongdu and the Prince of Jin Hongxi were both arrogant and reckless, while his youngest son the Prince of Yue Hongchang was filial, careful, and possessed wisdom and insight, he plotted with Right Vice Director and commissioner of the Western Inner Court Wang Hong to send Hongdu to garrison Yongzhou and Hongxi to garrison Rongzhou, and install Hongchang [as heir].
translations.idiomatic: As the Han Gaozu lay gravely ill, he judged his sons the Prince of Qin Hongdu and the Prince of Jin Hongxi to be proud and unrestrained, whereas his youngest son the Prince of Yue Hongchang was dutiful, circumspect, and capable. He conspired with Right Vice Director and commissioner of the Western Inner Court Wang Hong to post Hongdu to Yongzhou and Hongxi to Rongzhou while elevating Hongchang to succeed him.

sentences.zh: 制命將行，會崇文使蕭益入問疾，以其事訪之。

translations.literal: The order was about to be issued, when it happened that Commissioner for Promoting Culture Xiao Yi came to inquire after his illness; he consulted Yi on the matter.
translations.idiomatic: The decree was about to be issued when Commissioner for Promoting Culture Xiao Yi came to inquire after his health. The emperor consulted him on the plan.

sentences.zh: 益曰：「立嫡以長，違之必亂。」

translations.literal: Yi said: "Establish the heir by primogeniture of the legitimate line; to violate this will surely bring disorder."
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Yi said, "The heir should be the eldest son of the principal consort. To set that rule aside is to invite chaos."

sentences.zh: 乃止。

translations.literal: Thereupon it was halted.
translations.idiomatic: The plan was abandoned.

sentences.zh: 丁丑，高祖殂。

translations.literal: On dingchou, Gaozu died.
translations.idiomatic: On dingchou, Gaozu died.

sentences.zh: 高祖為人辨察，多權數，好自矜大，常謂中國天子為「洛州刺史」。

translations.literal: Gaozu as a man was penetrating in judgment, employed many stratagems, loved to vaunt himself, and often called the Son of Heaven of China "the prefect of Luozhou."
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu was sharp-witted and full of stratagem, fond of magnifying himself, and often referred to the Chinese Son of Heaven as "the Prefect of Luozhou."

sentences.zh: 嶺南珍異所聚，每窮奢極麗，宮殿悉以金玉珠翠為飾。

translations.literal: The exotic rarities of Lingnan gathered there; he always exhausted luxury to the utmost, and the palaces were all adorned with gold, jade, pearls, and kingfisher feathers.
translations.idiomatic: Exotic treasures of Lingnan filled his court, and he pursued extravagance to its limit. His palaces were adorned throughout with gold, jade, pearls, and kingfisher plumes.

sentences.zh: 用刑慘酷，有灌鼻、割舌、支解、刳剔、砲炙、烹蒸之法；

translations.literal: His use of punishments was savagely cruel; there were methods of pouring into the nose, cutting out the tongue, dismembering, excising and scooping, roasting over fire, and steaming in a cauldron;
translations.idiomatic: His punishments were unspeakably cruel—there were pourings into the nose, tongue-cuttings, dismemberments, excisions, slow roastings, and boilings alive—

sentences.zh: 或聚毒蛇水中，以罪人投之，謂之水獄。

translations.literal: sometimes poisonous snakes were gathered in water and the condemned thrown in; this was called the water prison.
translations.idiomatic: sometimes venomous serpents were gathered in a pool and condemned men cast in; this was called the Water Prison.

sentences.zh: 同平章事楊洞潛諫，不聽。

translations.literal: Co-administrator Yang Dongqian remonstrated; he would not listen.
translations.idiomatic: Co-administrator Yang Dongqian remonstrated against such practices, but the emperor would not heed him.

sentences.zh: 末年尤猜忌；

translations.literal: In his later years he was especially suspicious;
translations.idiomatic: In his final years he grew ever more suspicious;

sentences.zh: 以士人多為子孫計，故專任宦者，由是其國中宦者大盛。

translations.literal: because scholar-officials mostly planned for their descendants' sake, he therefore relied exclusively on eunuchs; hence eunuchs flourished greatly within his state.
translations.idiomatic: believing that scholar-officials served mainly to advance their own sons and grandsons, he entrusted power exclusively to eunuchs, and eunuchs accordingly rose to great dominance throughout his realm.

sentences.zh: 秦王弘度即皇帝位，更名玢。

translations.literal: The Prince of Qin Hongdu assumed the imperial throne and changed his name to Bin.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Qin Hongdu ascended the throne and changed his name to Bin.

sentences.zh: 以弘熙輔政，改元光天；

translations.literal: Hongxi was made to assist in government, and the era name was changed to Guangtian;
translations.idiomatic: Hongxi was appointed to assist in government, and the era name was changed to Guangtian;

sentences.zh: 尊母趙昭儀曰皇太妃。

translations.literal: His mother, Lady Zhao the Zhaoyi, was honored as Imperial Noble Consort.
translations.idiomatic: His mother, Lady Zhao the Zhaoyi, was honored as Imperial Noble Consort.

sentences.zh: 契丹以晉招納吐谷渾，遣使來讓。

translations.literal: The Khitan, because Jin had received and sheltered the Tuyuhun, dispatched envoys to remonstrate.
translations.idiomatic: Because Jin had offered refuge to the Tuyuhun, the Khitan sent envoys to lodge a protest.

sentences.zh: 帝憂悒不知為計；

translations.literal: The emperor was distressed and did not know what plan to adopt;
translations.idiomatic: The emperor brooded in distress, unable to devise a response;

sentences.zh: 五月，己亥，始有疾。

translations.literal: In the fifth month, on jihai, he first fell ill.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month, on jihai, he first fell ill.

sentences.zh: 乙巳，尊太妃劉氏為皇太后。

translations.literal: On yisi, Imperial Noble Consort Liu was honored as Empress Dowager.
translations.idiomatic: On yisi, Imperial Noble Consort Liu was honored as Empress Dowager.

sentences.zh: 太后，帝之庶母也。

translations.literal: The empress dowager was the emperor's concubine mother.
translations.idiomatic: The empress dowager was the emperor's stepmother.

sentences.zh: 唐丞相、太保宋齊丘既罷尚書省，不復朝謁。

translations.literal: Tang Grand Counselor and Grand Guardian Song Qiqiu, having been dismissed from the Department of State Affairs, no longer attended court audiences.
translations.idiomatic: Song Qiqiu, Tang grand counselor and grand guardian, having stepped down from the Department of State Affairs, ceased attending court audiences altogether.

sentences.zh: 唐主遣壽王景遂勞問，許鎮洪州，始入朝。

translations.literal: The Tang ruler sent Prince Jing of Shou to inquire after his comfort, promised him command at Hongzhou, and only then did he enter court.
translations.idiomatic: The Tang ruler sent Prince Jing of Shou to inquire after him, promised him a post at Hongzhou, and only then did Song Qiqiu return to court.

sentences.zh: 唐主與之宴，酒酣，齊丘曰：「陛下中興，臣之力也，奈何忘之！」

translations.literal: The Tang ruler banqueted with him; when the wine had gone deep, Qiqiu said: "Your Majesty's restoration was my achievement—how can you forget it!"
translations.idiomatic: The Tang ruler held a banquet for him. When the wine had gone deep, Qiqiu said, "Your Majesty's restoration was my doing—how can you forget it!"

sentences.zh: 唐主怒曰：「公以遊客干朕，今為三公，亦足矣。

translations.literal: The Tang ruler angrily said: "You as a wandering guest importuned me; now you are one of the Three Excellencies—is that not enough?
translations.idiomatic: The Tang ruler erupted in anger. "You came to me a mere wandering guest, and now you stand among the Three Excellencies—is that not enough?

sentences.zh: 乃與人言朕烏喙如句踐，難與共安樂，有之乎？」

translations.literal: Yet you tell others that I have a beak like Goujian and am hard to share joy with—is that so?"
translations.idiomatic: And yet you tell others I have Goujian's hooked beak and am impossible to enjoy peace with—is that not so?"

sentences.zh: 齊丘曰：「臣實有此言。

translations.literal: Qiqiu said: "Your servant truly said this.
translations.idiomatic: Qiqiu said, "I did speak those words, Your Majesty.

sentences.zh: 臣為遊客時，陛下乃偏裨耳。

translations.literal: When I was a wandering guest, Your Majesty was only a junior officer.
translations.idiomatic: When I was yet a wandering guest, Your Majesty was nothing but a junior officer.

sentences.zh: 今日殺臣可矣。」

translations.literal: Today you may kill your servant—that is enough."
translations.idiomatic: If Your Majesty wishes to kill me today, so be it."

sentences.zh: 明日，唐主手詔謝之曰：「朕之褊性，子嵩平昔所知。

translations.literal: The next day the Tang ruler wrote a personal edict of apology saying: "My narrow temperament—Zisong has long known it.
translations.idiomatic: The next day the Tang ruler sent a personal edict of apology: "My narrow temperament is something you have known well for years, Zisong.

sentences.zh: 少相親，老相怨，可乎！」

translations.literal: To be close when young and resentful when old—can that be?"
translations.idiomatic: Must we who were close in youth become estranged in old age?"

sentences.zh: 丙午，以齊丘為鎮南節度使。

translations.literal: On bingwu, Qiqiu was made military governor of Zhennan.
translations.idiomatic: On bingwu, Qiqiu was appointed military governor of Zhennan.

sentences.zh: 帝寢疾，一旦，馮道獨對。

translations.literal: The emperor lay gravely ill; one day Feng Dao alone attended him in audience.
translations.idiomatic: As the emperor lay gravely ill, Feng Dao once attended him in a private audience.

sentences.zh: 帝命幼子重睿出拜之，又令宦者抱重睿置道懷中，其意蓋欲道輔立之。

translations.literal: The emperor ordered his youngest son Chongrui to come out and bow to him, and further ordered a eunuch to hold Chongrui and place him in Dao's embrace; his intent was presumably to have Dao assist in installing him [as heir].
translations.idiomatic: The emperor summoned his youngest son Chongrui to bow before Feng Dao and had a eunuch place the boy in Feng Dao's arms—clearly intending that Feng Dao support his succession.

sentences.zh: 六月，乙丑，帝殂。

translations.literal: In the sixth month, on yichou, the emperor died.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month, on yichou, the emperor died.

sentences.zh: 道與天平節度使、侍衛馬步都虞候景延廣議，以國家多難，宜立長君，乃奉廣晉尹齊王重貴為嗣。

translations.literal: Feng Dao together with Tiansping military governor and commander of the palace horse-and-foot guards Jing Yanguang deliberated; because the state faced many troubles, the elder ruler should be established, and they then installed Qi Wang Chonggui, Guangjin Director, as successor.
translations.idiomatic: Feng Dao conferred with Tiansping military governor and commander of palace horse and foot Jing Yanguang. Judging the realm beset by troubles, they held that an elder and more seasoned ruler should be chosen, and together they installed Qi Wang Chonggui, the Guangjin Director, as heir.

sentences.zh: 是日，齊王即皇帝位。

translations.literal: That same day, Qi Wang assumed the imperial throne.
translations.idiomatic: That same day, Qi Wang ascended the throne.

sentences.zh: 延廣以為己功，始用事，禁都下人毋得偶語。

translations.literal: Yanguang considered it his own achievement and began to wield power, forbidding people in the capital from speaking in pairs.
translations.idiomatic: Jing Yanguang claimed credit for the outcome and began to wield power, forbidding anyone in the capital to speak together in pairs.

sentences.zh: 初，高祖疾亟，有旨召河東度使劉知遠入輔政，齊王寢之；

translations.literal: Initially, when Gaozu was critically ill, there was an order summoning Hedong military governor Liu Zhiyuan to enter and assist in government; Qi Wang suppressed it;
translations.idiomatic: When Gaozu first fell critically ill, he had issued an order summoning Hedong military governor Liu Zhiyuan to the capital to assist in government, but Qi Wang suppressed it;

sentences.zh: 知遠由是怨齊王。

translations.literal: Zhiyuan on this account resented Qi Wang.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Zhiyuan therefore came to resent Qi Wang.

sentences.zh: 丁卯，尊皇太后曰太皇太后，皇后曰皇太后。

translations.literal: On dingmao, the Empress Dowager was honored as Grand Empress Dowager, and the empress was honored as Empress Dowager.
translations.idiomatic: On dingmao, the empress dowager was elevated to grand empress dowager, and the empress was honored as empress dowager.

sentences.zh: 閩富沙王延政圍汀州，閩主曦發漳、泉兵五千救之。

translations.literal: Min Prince of Fusha Yan Zheng besieged Tingzhou; the Min ruler Xi dispatched five thousand troops from Zhang and Quan to rescue it.
translations.idiomatic: Min Prince of Fusha Yan Zheng besieged Tingzhou, and the Min ruler Xi sent five thousand troops from Zhang and Quan to its relief.

sentences.zh: 又遣其將林守亮入尤溪，大明宮使黃敬忠屯尤口，欲乘虛襲建州；

translations.literal: He also dispatched his general Lin Shouliang to enter Youxi, and Palace Commissioner Huang Jingzhong encamped at Youkou, intending to seize the opportunity to strike Jianzhou;
translations.idiomatic: He also sent his general Lin Shouliang into Youxi while Palace Commissioner Huang Jingzhong encamped at Youkou, planning to strike Jianzhou while the enemy's defenses were exposed;

sentences.zh: 國計使黃紹頗將步卒八千為二軍聲援。

translations.literal: State Planning Commissioner Huang Shaopo led eight thousand infantry as two armies in vocal support.
translations.idiomatic: State Planning Commissioner Huang Shaopo led eight thousand foot soldiers in two columns to reinforce them.

sentences.zh: 秋，七月，壬辰，太皇太后劉氏殂。

translations.literal: In autumn, the seventh month, on renchen, Grand Empress Dowager Liu died.
translations.idiomatic: In autumn, the seventh month, on renchen, Grand Empress Dowager Liu died.

sentences.zh: 閩富沙王延政攻汀州，四十二戰，不克而歸。

translations.literal: Min Prince of Fusha Yan Zheng attacked Tingzhou; after forty-two battles he could not capture it and returned.
translations.idiomatic: Min Prince of Fusha Yan Zheng assaulted Tingzhou. After forty-two engagements he failed to take the city and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 其將包洪實、陳望，將水軍以御福州之師；

translations.literal: His generals Bao Hongshi and Chen Wang led the water army to oppose the army from Fuzhou;
translations.idiomatic: His generals Bao Hongshi and Chen Wang commanded the river fleet to block the force advancing from Fuzhou;

sentences.zh: 丁酉，遇於尤口。

translations.literal: On dingyou, they encountered each other at Youkou.
translations.idiomatic: On dingyou, the two forces met at Youkou.

sentences.zh: 黃敬忠將戰，占者言時刻未利，按兵不動；

translations.literal: Huang Jingzhong was about to give battle; the diviner said the hour was not favorable, and he held the troops without moving;
translations.idiomatic: Huang Jingzhong prepared to give battle, but the diviner declared the hour unfavorable, and he held his troops in place;

sentences.zh: 洪實等引兵登岸，水陸夾攻之，殺敬忠，俘斬二千級，林守亮、黃紹頗皆遁歸。

translations.literal: Hongshi and the others led troops ashore; from water and land they attacked on both sides, killed Jingzhong, captured and beheaded two thousand enemies; Lin Shouliang and Huang Shaopo both fled back.
translations.idiomatic: Hongshi and his men came ashore and attacked from land and water at once. They killed Huang Jingzhong and killed or captured two thousand of the enemy. Lin Shouliang and Huang Shaopo both fled the field.

sentences.zh: 庚子，大赦。

translations.literal: On gengzi, a general amnesty was proclaimed.
translations.idiomatic: On gengzi, the court proclaimed a general amnesty.

sentences.zh: 癸卯，加景延廣同平章事，兼侍衛馬步都指揮使。

translations.literal: On guimao, Jing Yanguang was added as Tong Pingzhangshi, and concurrently made Commander of the Palace Guard Horse and Foot.
translations.idiomatic: On guimao, Jing Yanguang was promoted to co-equal chancellor and appointed commander-in-chief of the palace guard, horse and foot alike.

sentences.zh: 勳舊皆欲復置樞密使，馮道等三表，請以樞密舊職讓之；

translations.literal: Merit veterans all wished to restore the office of Privy Commissioner; Feng Dao and others submitted three memorials, requesting to yield the old Privy post to them;
translations.idiomatic: The old hands who had earned their merit all wanted the Privy Commission restored. Feng Dao and others sent up three memorials, offering to surrender their former Privy posts to them.

sentences.zh: 帝不許。

translations.literal: The emperor did not assent.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor refused.

sentences.zh: 有神降於博羅縣民家，與人言而不見其形，閭閻人往占吉凶，多驗，縣吏張遇賢事之甚謹。

translations.literal: A spirit descended at a commoner's home in Boluo County; it spoke with people but its form could not be seen; neighbors came to inquire about fortune and misfortune, and predictions often came true; the county clerk Zhang Yuxian served it with great reverence.
translations.idiomatic: A spirit descended into a household in Boluo County. It spoke with men and women yet showed no form. Neighbors flocked to it for auguries of fortune and ruin, and its words often proved true. The county clerk Zhang Yuxian tended it with scrupulous devotion.

sentences.zh: 時循州盜賊群起，莫相統一，賊帥共禱於神，神大言曰：「張遇賢當為汝主。」

translations.literal: At the time bandits rose in groups across Xun Prefecture, with no one to unify them; the bandit chiefs jointly prayed to the spirit; the spirit declared loudly: "Zhang Yuxian shall be your lord."
translations.idiomatic: Bandits were rising everywhere in Xun Prefecture, leaderless and scattered. The chiefs prayed together before the spirit, and it thundered: "Zhang Yuxian shall be your sovereign."

sentences.zh: 於是群帥共奉遇賢，稱中天八國王，改元永樂，置百官，攻掠海隅。

translations.literal: Thereupon the chiefs together installed Yuxian, styled him King of the Eight Kingdoms of the Middle Heaven, changed the era name to Yongle, established the full bureaucracy, and raided the coastal regions.
translations.idiomatic: At once the chiefs raised Yuxian up, hailed him King of the Eight Kingdoms of the Middle Heaven, proclaimed the era Yongle, set up a full court of offices, and swept the coast in plunder.

sentences.zh: 遇賢年少，無他方略，諸將但告進退而已。

translations.literal: Yuxian was young and had no other strategy; the generals merely reported advance or retreat to him.
translations.idiomatic: Yuxian was still young and knew no stratagem beyond this; his generals simply told him when to advance or withdraw.

sentences.zh: 漢主以越王弘昌為都統，循王弘杲為副以討之，戰於錢帛館。

translations.literal: The Han ruler appointed Prince Yue Hongchang as supreme commander and Prince Xun Honggao as his deputy to campaign against them; they fought at the Qianbo Pavilion.
translations.idiomatic: The Han sovereign sent Prince Yue Hongchang as supreme commander, with Prince Xun Honggao as his second, to suppress the rebellion. They gave battle at the Qianbo Pavilion.

sentences.zh: 漢兵不利，二王皆為賊所圍；

translations.literal: Han forces fared poorly; both princes were surrounded by the rebels;
translations.idiomatic: The Han army met defeat; both princes were hemmed in by the rebels.

sentences.zh: 指揮使陳道癢等力戰救之，得免。

translations.literal: Commander Chen Daoyang and others fought fiercely to rescue them, and they escaped.
translations.idiomatic: Commander Chen Daoyang and his men fought with desperate strength to break the encirclement, and the princes were saved.

sentences.zh: 東方州縣多為遇賢所陷。

translations.literal: Eastern prefectures and counties mostly fell to Yuxian.
translations.idiomatic: Prefectures and counties across the east largely fell into Yuxian's hands.

sentences.zh: 道庠，端州人也。

translations.literal: Daoxiang was a man of Duanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Daoxiang was native to Duanzhou.

sentences.zh: 高行周圍襄州逾年，不下。

translations.literal: Gao Xingzhou besieged Xiang Prefecture for more than a year without taking it.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Xingzhou invested Xiang Prefecture for over a year and could not bring it down.

sentences.zh: 城中食盡，奉國軍都虞候曲周王清言於行周曰：「賊城已危，我師已老，民力已困，不早迫之，尚何俟乎！」

translations.literal: Food in the city ran out; Wang Qing of Quzhou, deputy chief of the Fengguo Army, said to Xingzhou: "The rebel city is already perilous, our army is worn, civilian strength is exhausted—if we do not press the assault soon, what are we waiting for!"
translations.idiomatic: When provisions in the city were spent, Wang Qing of Quzhou, deputy chief of the Fengguo Army, urged Xingzhou: "The rebels' walls are already failing, our troops are weary, and the people's strength is spent. If we do not press the attack now, how long will we wait?"

sentences.zh: 與奉國都指揮使元城劉詞帥眾先登。

translations.literal: Together with Liu Ci of Yuancheng, commander of the Fengguo Army, he led the troops in scaling the walls first.
translations.idiomatic: He and Liu Ci of Yuancheng, commander of the Fengguo Army, stormed the walls at the head of the host.

sentences.zh: 八月，拔之。

translations.literal: In the eighth month, they took it.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month the city fell.

sentences.zh: 安從進舉族自焚。

translations.literal: An Congjin burned himself along with his entire clan.
translations.idiomatic: An Congjin gathered his whole clan and burned himself alive.

sentences.zh: 甲子，以趙瑩為中書令。

translations.literal: On jiazi, Zhao Ying was made Director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: On jiazi, Zhao Ying was appointed Director of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 閩主曦遣使以手詔及金器九百、錢萬緡、將吏敕告六百四十通，求和於富沙王延政，延政不受。

translations.literal: The Min ruler Xi sent envoys with an autograph edict, nine hundred gold vessels, ten thousand strings of cash, and six hundred forty imperial commissions for officers, seeking peace from Prince Fusha Yan Zheng; Yan Zheng refused.
translations.idiomatic: The Min ruler Xi dispatched envoys bearing his own hand-edict, nine hundred gold vessels, ten thousand strings of cash, and six hundred forty sealed commissions for officers and men, suing for peace with Prince Fusha Yan Zheng. Yan Zheng would not accept.

sentences.zh: 丙寅，閩主曦宴群臣於九龍殿。

translations.literal: On bingyin, the Min ruler Xi feasted his ministers in the Hall of Nine Dragons.
translations.idiomatic: On bingyin the Min ruler Xi held a banquet for his ministers in the Hall of Nine Dragons.

sentences.zh: 從子繼柔不能飲，強之。

translations.literal: His nephew Jirou could not drink; they forced him.
translations.idiomatic: His nephew Jirou could not hold his wine, but they pressed him to drink all the same.

sentences.zh: 繼柔私減其酒，曦怒，並客將斬之。

translations.literal: Jirou secretly diluted his wine; Xi grew angry and beheaded him along with the attending officer.
translations.idiomatic: Jirou secretly watered down his cup. Xi flew into a rage and had him beheaded, together with the officer who had been his guest.

sentences.zh: 閩人鑄永隆通寶大鐵錢，一當鉛錢百。

translations.literal: The people of Min cast large iron coins called Yonglong Tongbao, each worth one hundred lead coins.
translations.idiomatic: Min cast great iron coins bearing the inscription Yonglong Tongbao, each valued at a hundred lead coins.

sentences.zh: 漢葬天皇大帝於康陵，廟號高祖。

translations.literal: Han buried the Heavenly Sovereign Emperor at Kangling; temple name Gaozu.
translations.idiomatic: Han interred the Heavenly Sovereign Emperor at Kangling and gave him the temple name Gaozu.

sentences.zh: 唐主自為吳相，興利除害，變更舊法甚多。

translations.literal: Since serving as Wu's chancellor, the Tang ruler had promoted benefits and removed harms, changing many old laws.
translations.idiomatic: From the time he served Wu as chancellor, the Tang ruler had sought profit for the people and cleared away abuses, altering a great many old statutes.

sentences.zh: 及即位，命法官及尚書刪定為《升元條》三十卷；

translations.literal: Upon acceding, he ordered judicial officers and the Secretariat to compile and revise them into thirty scrolls titled the Shengyuan Articles;
translations.idiomatic: When he took the throne, he commanded judicial officers and the Secretariat to edit and codify them into thirty scrolls, the Shengyuan Articles.

sentences.zh: 庚寅，行之。

translations.literal: On gengyin, they were implemented.
translations.idiomatic: On gengyin the code took effect.

sentences.zh: 閩主曦以同平章事候官余廷英為泉州刺史。

translations.literal: The Min ruler Xi appointed Yu Tingying of Houguan, co-equal chancellor, as prefect of Quanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: The Min ruler Xi made Yu Tingying of Houguan, his co-equal chancellor, prefect of Quanzhou.

sentences.zh: 廷英貪穢，掠人女子，詐稱受詔采擇以備後宮。

translations.literal: Tingying was greedy and corrupt; he seized people's daughters, falsely claiming he had received orders to select them for the rear palace.
translations.idiomatic: Tingying was grasping and corrupt. He seized men's daughters, pretending he had been commanded to gather them for the inner palace.

sentences.zh: 事覺，曦遣御史按之。

translations.literal: When the matter came to light, Xi sent censors to investigate.
translations.idiomatic: When the affair was exposed, Xi dispatched censors to investigate.

sentences.zh: 廷英懼，詣福州自歸，曦詰責，將以屬吏；

translations.literal: Tingying was afraid and came to Fuzhou to surrender; Xi interrogated and reproached him, intending to hand him over to the law officers;
translations.idiomatic: Tingying, in fear, came to Fuzhou to give himself up. Xi questioned and rebuked him, and was about to remand him to the magistrates.

sentences.zh: 廷英退，獻買宴錢萬緡。

translations.literal: Tingying withdrew and presented ten thousand strings of cash as purchase money for a banquet.
translations.idiomatic: Tingying withdrew and offered ten thousand strings of cash as the price of a feast.

sentences.zh: 曦悅，明日召見，謂曰：「宴已買矣，皇后貢物安在？」

translations.literal: Xi was pleased; the next day he summoned him and said: "The banquet has been bought—where are the empress's tribute goods?"
translations.idiomatic: Xi was delighted. The next day he summoned Tingying and said, "The feast is paid for—where is the empress's tribute?"

sentences.zh: 廷英復獻錢於李後，乃遣歸泉州；

translations.literal: Tingying again presented cash to Empress Li, whereupon Xi sent him back to Quanzhou;
translations.idiomatic: Tingying paid out again, this time to Empress Li, and only then was he sent back to Quanzhou.

sentences.zh: 自是諸州皆別貢皇后物。

translations.literal: From then on, every prefecture separately presented tribute goods for the empress.
translations.idiomatic: After that, every prefecture began sending separate tribute for the empress.

sentences.zh: 未幾，復召廷英為相。

translations.literal: Before long, Xi summoned Tingying back as chancellor.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Xi recalled Tingying to serve again as chancellor.

sentences.zh: 冬，十月，丙子，張遇賢陷循州，殺漢刺史劉傳。

translations.literal: In winter, the tenth month, on bingzi, Zhang Yuxian took Xun Prefecture and killed Han prefect Liu Chuan.
translations.idiomatic: In winter, the tenth month, on bingzi, Zhang Yuxian seized Xun Prefecture and slew the Han prefect Liu Chuan.

sentences.zh: 楚王希範作天策府，極棟宇之盛；

translations.literal: King of Chu Ma Xifan built the Celestial Policies Bureau, making the architecture magnificently grand;
translations.idiomatic: Ma Xifan, King of Chu, raised the Celestial Policies Bureau, lavishing every extravagance upon its halls and towers.

sentences.zh: 戶牖欄檻皆飾以金玉，塗壁用丹砂數十萬斤；

translations.literal: Doors, windows, railings, and balustrades were all adorned with gold and jade; walls were coated with several hundred thousand jin of cinnabar.
translations.idiomatic: Doors, windows, rails, and balustrades glittered with gold and jade; the walls were painted with cinnabar by the hundred thousand jin.

sentences.zh: 地衣，春夏用角簟，秋冬用木綿。

translations.literal: For floor coverings, horn mats in spring and summer, cotton in autumn and winter.
translations.idiomatic: The floor coverings were horn mats in spring and summer, cotton in autumn and winter.

sentences.zh: 與子弟僚屬游宴其間。

translations.literal: He toured and feasted there with his sons, younger brothers, and staff.
translations.idiomatic: There he wandered and feasted with his sons, younger brothers, and the officers of his court.

sentences.zh: 十一月，庚寅，葬聖文章武明德孝皇帝於顯陵，廟號高祖。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month, on gengyin, the Sacred Literary Martial Virtuous Filial Emperor was buried at Xianling; temple name Gaozu.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month, on gengyin, the Sacred Literary Martial Virtuous Filial Emperor was laid to rest at Xianling and given the temple name Gaozu.

sentences.zh: 先是，河南、北諸州官自賣海鹽，歲收緡錢十七萬；

translations.literal: Previously, prefectures north and south of the Yellow River sold sea salt on their own, collecting one hundred seventy thousand strings per year;
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, the prefectures north and south of the Yellow River had sold sea salt themselves, taking in one hundred seventy thousand strings a year.

sentences.zh: 又散蠶鹽斂民錢。

translations.literal: They also distributed silkworm salt to levy money from the people.
translations.idiomatic: They also scattered silkworm salt among the people and collected money in return.

sentences.zh: 言事者稱民坐私販鹽抵罪者眾，不若聽民自販，而歲以官所賣錢直斂於民，謂之食鹽錢；

translations.literal: Memorialists said many people were punished for private salt trafficking; it would be better to let people sell freely, while collecting the annual revenue the government had gained from salt sales directly from the people—a levy called the salt-consumption tax;
translations.idiomatic: Memorialists argued that countless commoners were being punished for trafficking in salt on their own. Better, they said, to let the people trade freely, while the state each year collected from them the sum it had once earned from official sales—a charge called the salt-consumption tax.

sentences.zh: 高祖從之。

translations.literal: Gaozu assented.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu agreed.

sentences.zh: 俄而鹽價頓賤，每斤至十錢。

translations.literal: Before long salt prices collapsed, to as low as ten cash per jin.
translations.idiomatic: Soon salt plunged in price, falling as low as ten cash per jin.

sentences.zh: 至是，三司使董遇欲增求羨利，而難於驟變前法，乃重征鹽商，過者七錢，留賣者十錢。

translations.literal: At this time, Commissioner of the Three Departments Dong Yu wished to increase surplus profit but found it hard to suddenly alter the prior law; he therefore heavily taxed salt merchants—seven cash for those passing through, ten for those who stayed to sell.
translations.idiomatic: By then the Commissioner of the Three Departments, Dong Yu, wanted to squeeze out greater profit yet shrank from overturning the new law at a stroke. Instead he piled heavy duties on salt merchants: seven cash on those merely passing through, ten on those who lingered to sell.

sentences.zh: 由是鹽商殆絕，而官復自賣。

translations.literal: Thereupon salt merchants nearly disappeared, and the government resumed selling salt itself.
translations.idiomatic: Salt merchants all but vanished, and the state once again took up selling salt on its own account.

sentences.zh: 其食鹽錢，至今斂之如故。

translations.literal: The salt-consumption tax—collection continued as before down to the present.
translations.idiomatic: As for the salt-consumption tax, it was still levied unchanged.

sentences.zh: 閩鹽鐵使、右僕射李仁遇，敏之子，閩主曦之甥也；

translations.literal: Li Renyu, Min commissioner of salt and iron and right vice director of the Secretariat, was the son of Min and the Min ruler Xi's nephew;
translations.idiomatic: Li Renyu, Min's commissioner of salt and iron and right vice director of the Secretariat, was Min's son and nephew to the Min ruler Xi.

sentences.zh: 年少，美姿容，得幸於曦。

translations.literal: Young, handsome in bearing, he won Xi's favor.
translations.idiomatic: He was young and fair of face, and won Xi's special favor.

sentences.zh: 十二月，以仁遇為左僕射兼中書侍郎，翰林學士、吏部侍郎李光准為中書侍郎兼戶部尚書，並同平章事。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month, Renyu was made left vice director and concurrently vice director of the Secretariat; Hanlin academician and vice minister of Personnel Li Guangzhun was made vice director of the Secretariat and concurrent minister of Revenue—both as co-equal chancellors.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month Renyu was made left vice director and vice director of the Secretariat; Hanlin academician and vice minister of Personnel Li Guangzhun was made vice director of the Secretariat and minister of Revenue. Both were appointed co-equal chancellors.

sentences.zh: 曦荒淫無度，嘗夜宴，光准醉忤旨，命執送都市斬之；

translations.literal: Xi was debauched without limit; once at a night feast, Guangzhun, drunken, offended him; Xi ordered him seized and sent to the market for execution;
translations.idiomatic: Xi abandoned himself to pleasure without measure. One night at banquet Guangzhun, drunk, gave offense. Xi ordered him seized and marched to the execution ground.

sentences.zh: 吏不敢殺，系獄中。

translations.literal: The officers dared not kill him; they imprisoned him.
translations.idiomatic: The officers did not dare carry out the sentence; they locked him in prison instead.

sentences.zh: 明日，視朝，召復其位。

translations.literal: The next day, when Xi held court, he summoned Guangzhun back to his post.
translations.idiomatic: The next morning, when Xi held audience, he restored Guangzhun to office.

sentences.zh: 是夕，又宴，收翰林學士周維岳下獄。

translations.literal: That same evening, at another feast, he had Hanlin academician Zhou Weiyue thrown into prison.
translations.idiomatic: That very evening, at yet another feast, he had the Hanlin academician Zhou Weiyue thrown into jail.

sentences.zh: 吏拂榻待之，曰：「相公昨夜宿此，尚書勿憂。」

translations.literal: The officers dusted off a couch for him and said: "Chancellor, you slept here last night—Minister, do not worry."
translations.idiomatic: The jailers brushed off a couch and told him, "Chancellor, you slept here last night, Minister—have no fear."

sentences.zh: 醒而釋之。

translations.literal: When Xi sobered, he released him.
translations.idiomatic: When Xi woke sober, he set Weiyue free.

sentences.zh: 他日，又宴，侍臣皆以醉去，獨維岳在。

translations.literal: Another day at a feast, the attending ministers all left drunk—Weiyue alone remained.
translations.idiomatic: On another night of feasting, every attendant minister staggered off drunk save Weiyue alone.

sentences.zh: 曦曰：「維岳身甚小，何飲酒之多？」

translations.literal: Xi said: "Weiyue's body is so small—how can he drink so much?"
translations.idiomatic: Xi said, "Weiyue is so slight of frame—how does he hold so much wine?"

sentences.zh: 左右或曰：「酒有別腸，不必長大。」

translations.literal: Someone nearby said: "Wine has its own separate gut; one need not be large."
translations.idiomatic: Someone at his side answered, "Wine runs through a separate gut; a man need not be tall to drink deep."

sentences.zh: 曦欣然，命捽維岳下殿，欲剖視其酒腸。

translations.literal: Xi was delighted and ordered Weiyue dragged down from the hall, intending to cut him open and examine his wine-gut.
translations.idiomatic: Xi laughed with pleasure and ordered Weiyue hauled down from the hall, intending to cut him open and inspect this wine-gut of his.

sentences.zh: 或曰：「殺維岳，無人復能侍陛下劇飲者。」

translations.literal: " Someone said: "If you kill Weiyue, there will be no one left who can keep pace with Your Majesty's heavy drinking."
translations.idiomatic: " Another voice said, "Slay Weiyue, and who will ever again keep Your Majesty company in deep drinking?"

sentences.zh: 乃捨之。

translations.literal: Xi then let him go.
translations.idiomatic: Xi stayed his hand and spared him.

sentences.zh: 帝之初即位也，大臣議奉表稱臣告哀於契丹，景延廣請致書稱孫而不稱臣。

translations.literal: When the emperor first took the throne, ministers discussed submitting a memorial addressing themselves as subjects to announce mourning to the Khitan; Jing Yanguang proposed instead sending a letter styling himself "grandson" but not "subject."
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of his reign the emperor's ministers debated whether to submit a memorial as vassals announcing the late emperor's death to the Khitan. Jing Yanguang urged that the letter call him "grandson" but not "subject."

sentences.zh: 李崧曰：「屈身以為社稷，何恥之有！

translations.literal: Li Song said: "To humble oneself for the sake of the state—what shame is there in that!
translations.idiomatic: Li Song said, "To bend the knee for the realm's sake—what shame lies in that?

sentences.zh: 陛下如此，他日必躬擐甲冑，與契丹戰，於時悔無益矣。」

translations.literal: If Your Majesty acts thus, one day you will surely don armor yourself and fight the Khitan—then regret will avail nothing."
translations.idiomatic: If Your Majesty goes this way, the day will come when you must buckle on armor yourself and meet the Khitan in battle—and then remorse will be too late."

sentences.zh: 延廣固爭，馮道依違其間。

translations.literal: Yanguang stood firm; Feng Dao wavered between them.
translations.idiomatic: Yanguang held his ground; Feng Dao hung undecided between the two.

sentences.zh: 帝卒從延廣議。

translations.literal: The emperor ultimately followed Yanguang's proposal.
translations.idiomatic: In the end the emperor sided with Yanguang.

sentences.zh: 契丹大怒，遣使來責讓，且言：「何得不先承稟，遽即帝位？」

translations.literal: The Khitan flew into rage and sent envoys to rebuke him, saying moreover: "How could you assume the throne without first seeking leave?"
translations.idiomatic: The Khitan ruler erupted in fury and sent envoys to upbraid him, demanding, "How dare you mount the throne without first seeking our leave?"

sentences.zh: 延廣復以不遜語答之。

translations.literal: Yanguang again answered with insolent words.
translations.idiomatic: Yanguang answered once more with words of defiance.

sentences.zh: 契丹盧龍節度使趙延壽欲代晉帝中國，屢說契丹擊晉，契丹主頗然之。

translations.literal: Zhao Yanshou, Khitan military governor of Lulong, wished to replace the Jin emperor in China; he repeatedly urged the Khitan ruler to strike Jin—and the Khitan ruler largely agreed.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Yanshou, the Khitan military governor of Lulong, meant to supplant the Jin emperor and rule China himself. Again and again he pressed the Khitan ruler to attack Jin, and the Khitan ruler was much inclined to listen.

sentences.zh: 齊王上

translations.literal: Volume One of King Qi
translations.idiomatic: King Qi, Part One

sentences.zh: 高祖聖文章武明德孝皇帝下天福八年（

translations.literal: Below: Gaozu the Sacred Literary Martial Virtuous Filial Emperor—Year Eight of Tianfu (
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu the Sacred Literary Martial Virtuous Filial Emperor, continued—Year Eight of Tianfu (

sentences.zh: 癸卯，公元九四三年）

translations.literal: guimao, AD 943)
translations.idiomatic: guimao, AD 943)

sentences.zh: 春，正月，癸卯，蜀主以宣徽使兼宮苑使田敬全領永平節度使；

translations.literal: In spring, the first month, on guimao, the Shu ruler appointed Xuanhui commissioner and concurrent palace park commissioner Tian Jingquan to hold the Yongping military commission;
translations.idiomatic: In spring, the first month, on guimao, the Shu ruler put Xuanhui commissioner and palace park commissioner Tian Jingquan in charge of the Yongping military commission.

sentences.zh: 敬全，宦者也，引前蜀王承休為比而命之，國人非之。

translations.literal: Jingquan was a eunuch; citing Former Shu king Wang Chengxiu as precedent in appointing him—the people of Shu disapproved.
translations.idiomatic: Jingquan was a eunuch. The ruler justified the appointment by pointing to Former Shu's Wang Chengxiu—and the people of Shu murmured against it.

sentences.zh: 帝聞契丹將入寇，二月，己未，發鄴都；

translations.literal: The emperor heard the Khitan were about to invade; in the second month, on jiwei, he departed Yedu;
translations.idiomatic: Learning that the Khitan were poised to invade, the emperor in the second month, on jiwei, set out from Yedu.

sentences.zh: 乙丑，至東京。

translations.literal: On yichou, he reached the Eastern Capital.
translations.idiomatic: On yichou he arrived at the Eastern Capital.

sentences.zh: 然猶與契丹問遺相往來，無虛月。

translations.literal: Yet gifts and messages still passed between him and the Khitan—not a month went without exchange.
translations.idiomatic: Even so, courtesies and gifts still shuttled back and forth with the Khitan—not a month passed without some embassy.

sentences.zh: 唐宣城王景達，剛毅開爽，烈祖愛之，屢欲以為嗣；

translations.literal: Tang's Prince of Xuancheng Jing Da was resolute, open-hearted, and frank; Liezu loved him and repeatedly wished to make him heir;
translations.idiomatic: Jing Da, Prince of Xuancheng, was firm, open, and forthright. Liezu doted on him and more than once meant to name him heir.

sentences.zh: 宋齊丘亟稱其才，唐主以齊王璟年長而止。

translations.literal: Song Qiqiu praised his talent at every turn; the Tang ruler stopped because Prince Qi Li Jing was the elder.
translations.idiomatic: Song Qiqiu never ceased praising his gifts, but the Tang ruler held back because Prince Qi Li Jing was the elder son.

sentences.zh: 璟以是怨齊丘。

translations.literal: Li Jing therefore resented Qiqiu.
translations.idiomatic: From this Li Jing came to bear Qiqiu a grudge.

sentences.zh: 唐主幼子景逷，母种氏有寵，齊王璟母宋皇后稀得進見。

translations.literal: Tang's youngest son Jing Ti—his mother the Lady Chong was favored; Li Jing's mother Empress Song rarely gained audience.
translations.idiomatic: The Tang ruler's youngest son, Jing Ti, was born to the favored Lady Chong, while Li Jing's mother, Empress Song, was seldom admitted to audience.

sentences.zh: 唐主如璟宮，遇璟親調樂器，大怒，誚讓者數日。

translations.literal: The Tang ruler went to Li Jing's palace and found Li Jing personally tuning instruments; he flew into rage and rebuked him for days.
translations.idiomatic: When the Tang ruler visited Li Jing's palace and found him tuning instruments with his own hands, he blazed with anger and upbraided him for days on end.

sentences.zh: 种氏乘間言，景逷雖幼而慧，可以為嗣。

translations.literal: Lady Chong seized an opening to say that though Jing Ti was young, he was clever and could serve as heir.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Chong seized the moment to say that though Jing Ti was still young, he was clever and fit to be heir.

sentences.zh: 唐主怒曰：「子有過，父訓之，常事也。

translations.literal: The Tang ruler angrily said: "When a son errs, the father instructs him—that is ordinary.
translations.idiomatic: The Tang ruler snapped, "When a son missteps, the father corrects him—that is only natural.

sentences.zh: 國家大計，女子何得預知！」

translations.literal: On great affairs of state, how may a woman presume to know beforehand!"
translations.idiomatic: Great affairs of state are no business for a woman to speak of!"

sentences.zh: 即命嫁之。

translations.literal: He immediately ordered her married off.
translations.idiomatic: He at once commanded that she be given in marriage and sent away.

sentences.zh: 唐主嘗夢吞靈丹，旦而方士史守沖獻丹方，以為神而餌之，浸成躁急。

translations.literal: The Tang ruler once dreamed he swallowed an immortal elixir; at dawn the daoist Shi Shouchong presented an elixir formula; taking it for miraculous, he consumed it—and gradually grew irritable and restless.
translations.idiomatic: The Tang ruler once dreamed that he swallowed an elixir of immortality. At dawn the daoist Shi Shouchong offered him a recipe. The ruler took it for a divine gift and began to ingest it, and little by little his temper turned sharp and fevered.

sentences.zh: 左右諫，不聽。

translations.literal: His attendants remonstrated; he would not listen.
translations.idiomatic: Those around him pleaded with him to stop; he would not hear them.

sentences.zh: 嘗以藥賜李建勳，建勳曰：「臣餌之數日，已覺躁熱，況多餌乎！」

translations.literal: Once he bestowed the medicine on Li Jianxun; Jianxun said: "Your servant took it for several days and already felt feverish agitation—how much more if one takes much!"
translations.idiomatic: Once he gave the drug to Li Jianxun. Jianxun said, "I took it for only a few days and already felt hot restlessness—what if one swallowed it in quantity?"

sentences.zh: 唐主曰：「朕服之久矣。」

translations.literal: The Tang ruler said: "I have taken it for a long while already."
translations.idiomatic: The Tang ruler answered, "I have been taking it a long time."

sentences.zh: 群臣奏事，往往暴怒；

translations.literal: When ministers presented business he often exploded in wrath;
translations.idiomatic: When his ministers came before him with business, he would often burst into rage.

sentences.zh: 然或有正色論辨中理者，亦斂容慰謝而從之。

translations.literal: Yet if someone argued with stern countenance and sound reason, he also composed himself, apologized in consolation, and followed their counsel.
translations.idiomatic: Yet if a man stood his ground with sober face and right reason, the ruler would also collect himself, offer gracious words, and yield.

sentences.zh: 唐主問道士王棲霞：「何道可致太平？」

translations.literal: The Tang ruler asked the daoist Wang Qixia: "By what Way may one bring about great peace?"
translations.idiomatic: The Tang ruler asked the daoist Wang Qixia, "By what Way can one bring the realm to great peace?"

sentences.zh: 對曰：「王者治心治身，乃治家國。

translations.literal: He replied: "A king who governs his heart and body—that is how one governs family and realm.
translations.idiomatic: Wang answered, "A king must first govern his own heart and body; only then can he govern house and realm.

sentences.zh: 今陛下尚未能去饑嗔、飽喜，何論太平！」

translations.literal: Now Your Majesty has not yet been able to cast off hunger-anger and satiety-joy—how speak of great peace!"
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty has not yet learned to leave off anger in hunger and delight in fullness—how then speak of great peace!"

sentences.zh: 宋-{后}-自簾中稱歎，以為至言。

translations.literal: Empress Song from behind the curtain cried admiration, calling it the utmost truth.
translations.idiomatic: From behind the curtain Empress Song cried out in praise, declaring it the truest word she had ever heard.

sentences.zh: 凡唐主所賜予，棲霞皆不受。

translations.literal: Whenever the Tang ruler bestowed gifts, Qixia would accept none of them.
translations.idiomatic: Whatever the Southern Tang emperor offered him, Qixia refused to take it.

sentences.zh: 棲霞常為人奏章，唐主欲為之築壇。

translations.literal: Qixia often submitted memorials on others' behalf, and the Tang ruler wished to build an altar for him.
translations.idiomatic: Qixia frequently drafted memorials for other people, and the emperor wanted to erect an altar in his honor.

sentences.zh: 辭曰：「國用方乏，何暇及此！

translations.literal: He declined, saying, "The state's revenues are already strained—how could we spare effort for this!
translations.idiomatic: He declined, saying, "The treasury is already empty. How can we afford such a thing?

sentences.zh: 俟焚章不化，乃當奏請耳。」

translations.literal: Wait until the burning of the memorial fails to consume it—only then should one submit the request."
translations.idiomatic: Wait until a burned memorial is left unconsumed by the flames. Only then will I ask for it."

sentences.zh: 駕部郎中馮延己，為齊王元帥府常書記，性傾巧，與宋齊丘及宣徽副使陳覺相結；

translations.literal: Feng Yanji, Director of the Directorate of Imperial Carriages, served as permanent secretary in the Prince of Qi's commandery headquarters. By nature he was artful and scheming, and he formed a clique with Song Qiqiu and Chen Jue, Deputy Commissioner of the Palace Secretariat;
translations.idiomatic: Feng Yanji of the Directorate of Imperial Carriages served as permanent secretary in the Prince of Qi's headquarters. Cunning by nature, he joined forces with Song Qiqiu and Chen Jue, deputy commissioner of the Palace Secretariat;

sentences.zh: 同府在巳上者，延己稍以計逐之。

translations.literal: those in the same office who ranked above him, Yanji gradually drove out by stratagem.
translations.idiomatic: any colleague in the same office who outranked him, Feng Yanji gradually maneuvered out of the way.

sentences.zh: 延已嘗戲謂中書侍郎孫晟曰：「公有何能，為中書郎？」

translations.literal: Yanji once jestingly said to Sun Sheng, Vice Director of the Secretariat, "What ability do you possess, that you hold the post of Secretariat Gentleman?"
translations.idiomatic: Feng Yanji once teased Sun Sheng, vice director of the Secretariat: "What talent do you have that qualifies you to be a secretariat gentleman?"

sentences.zh: 晟曰：「晟，山東鄙儒，文章不如公，詼諧不如公，諂詐不如公。

translations.literal: Sun Sheng said, "Sheng is a crude scholar from east of the mountains. In literary composition I am not your equal, in wit I am not your equal, in flattery and deceit I am not your equal.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Sheng replied, "I am only a rustic scholar from Shandong. I cannot match you in prose, in wit, or in sycophancy and deceit.

sentences.zh: 然主上使公與齊王游處，蓋欲以仁義輔導之也，豈但為聲色狗馬之友邪！

translations.literal: Yet the sovereign assigned you to keep company with the Prince of Qi, surely intending that you should guide him with benevolence and righteousness—how could it be merely to be a companion in music, women, dogs, and horses!
translations.idiomatic: But His Majesty paired you with the Prince of Qi so that you might guide him with virtue and righteousness. Surely he did not mean for you to be a companion in pleasure, horses, and hounds alone!

sentences.zh: 晟誠無能；

translations.literal: Sheng truly has no ability;
translations.idiomatic: I truly have no talent;

sentences.zh: 如公之能，適足為國家之禍耳。」

translations.literal: abilities such as yours are precisely enough to become the state's calamity."
translations.idiomatic: but talents like yours are exactly what can bring a nation to ruin."

sentences.zh: 延己，歙州人也。

translations.literal: Yanji was a man of She Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Feng Yanji was a native of Shezhou.

sentences.zh: 又有魏岑者，亦在齊王府。

translations.literal: There was also a Wei Cen, who likewise served in the Prince of Qi's household.
translations.idiomatic: There was also a Wei Cen, who served in the Prince of Qi's household as well.

sentences.zh: 給事中常夢錫屢言陳覺、馮延己、魏岑皆佞邪小人，不宜侍東宮；

translations.literal: Chang Mengxi, Supervising Secretary, repeatedly said that Chen Jue, Feng Yanji, and Wei Cen were all sycophantic and wicked petty men, unfit to attend the Eastern Palace;
translations.idiomatic: Chang Mengxi, a supervising secretary, repeatedly warned that Chen Jue, Feng Yanji, and Wei Cen were flatterers and villains who should not attend the crown prince;

sentences.zh: 司門郎中判大理寺蕭儼表稱陳覺奸回亂政；

translations.literal: Xiao Yan, Director of the Ministry of Justice acting as judge of the Court of Judicial Review, submitted a memorial declaring Chen Jue treacherous, perverse, and disruptive to government;
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Yan of the Ministry of Justice, serving concurrently as judge of the Court of Judicial Review, submitted a memorial accusing Chen Jue of treachery and corrupting the administration;

sentences.zh: 唐主頗感悟，未及去。

translations.literal: the Tang ruler was somewhat moved to understanding, but had not yet removed them.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was somewhat persuaded, but had not yet removed them from office.

sentences.zh: 會疽發背，秘不令人知，密令醫治之，聽政如故。

translations.literal: It happened that a carbuncle broke out on his back. He kept it secret and would not let anyone know, secretly ordering physicians to treat it, while conducting affairs of state as before.
translations.idiomatic: Then a carbuncle erupted on his back. He kept it secret, had physicians treat it quietly, and continued to hold court as usual.

sentences.zh: 庚午，疾亟，太醫吳廷裕遣親信召齊王璟入侍疾。

translations.literal: On gengwu, his illness became critical. The Chief Imperial Physician Wu Tingyu sent a trusted messenger to summon the Prince of Qi, Jing, to attend him in his illness.
translations.idiomatic: On the day gengwu his condition turned critical. Chief Imperial Physician Wu Tingyu sent a trusted messenger to summon Prince Qi Jing to his bedside.

sentences.zh: 唐主謂璟曰：「吾餌金石，始欲益壽，乃更傷生，汝宜戒之！」

translations.literal: The Tang ruler said to Jing, "I took mineral elixirs, intending at first to prolong life, yet they only further harmed my life. You should take warning from this!"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor told Jing, "I took mineral elixirs hoping to extend my life, but they only shortened it. You must guard against this!"

sentences.zh: 是夕，殂。

translations.literal: That evening, he died.
translations.idiomatic: That night he died.

sentences.zh: 秘不發喪，下制：「以齊王監國，大赦。」

translations.literal: They kept the death secret and did not announce mourning. An edict was issued: "Let the Prince of Qi supervise the state, and grant a general amnesty."
translations.idiomatic: The death was kept secret and mourning was not announced. An edict was issued: "The Prince of Qi shall serve as regent. A general amnesty is granted."

sentences.zh: 孫晟恐馮延己等用事，欲稱遺詔令太后臨朝稱制。

translations.literal: Sun Sheng, fearing that Feng Yanji and the others would wield power, wished to cite the testamentary edict to have the Empress Dowager attend court and hold regency.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Sheng, fearing that Feng Yanji and his faction would seize power, wanted to invoke the late emperor's edict and have the empress dowager assume regency.

sentences.zh: 翰林學士李貽業曰：「先帝嘗云：『婦人預政，亂之本也。』

translations.literal: Hanlin Academician Li Yiye said, "The late emperor once said, 'When women participate in government, that is the root of disorder.
translations.idiomatic: Hanlin academician Li Yiye said, "The late emperor once declared, 'When women meddle in government, that is the root of chaos.

sentences.zh: 安肯自為厲階！

translations.literal: How could he willingly create the very cause of calamity himself!
translations.idiomatic: How could he have chosen to become the author of his own ruin!

sentences.zh: 此必近習奸人之詐也。

translations.literal: This must be the fraud of close attendants and wicked men.
translations.idiomatic: This must be a forgery by court favorites and schemers.

sentences.zh: 且嗣君春秋已長，明德著聞，公何得遽為亡國之言！

translations.literal: Moreover, the heir is already grown in years, and his virtue is well known. How can you so hastily speak words that would destroy the state!
translations.idiomatic: Besides, the heir is already a grown man of proven virtue. How can you so rashly utter words that would ruin the realm!

sentences.zh: 若果宣行，吾必對百官毀之。」

translations.literal: If this is truly proclaimed and carried out, I shall certainly tear it apart before the assembled officials."
translations.idiomatic: If this edict is actually promulgated, I will denounce it before the whole court."

sentences.zh: 晟懼而止。

translations.literal: Sheng, in fear, desisted.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Sheng, alarmed, abandoned the plan.

sentences.zh: 貽業，蔚之從曾孫也。

translations.literal: Yiye was a great-great-grandson of Wei, by a collateral line.
translations.idiomatic: Li Yiye was a collateral descendant of Li Wei.

sentences.zh: 丙子，始宣遺制。

translations.literal: On bingzi, the testamentary institutions were first proclaimed.
translations.idiomatic: On the day bingzi the late emperor's final edicts were publicly announced.

sentences.zh: 烈祖末年卞急，近臣多罹譴罰。

translations.literal: In his final years the Founding Emperor was impatient and severe; close ministers often suffered reprimand and punishment.
translations.idiomatic: In his last years the Founding Emperor had grown harsh and quick-tempered, and many of his close ministers were punished.

sentences.zh: 陳覺稱疾，累月不入，及宣遺詔，乃出。

translations.literal: Chen Jue claimed illness and for many months did not enter court; only when the testamentary edict was proclaimed did he emerge.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Jue pleaded illness and stayed away from court for months, appearing only after the testamentary edict was announced.

sentences.zh: 蕭儼劾奏：「覺端居私室，以俟升遐，請按其罪。」

translations.literal: Xiao Yan submitted an impeachment: "Jue sat quietly in his private chamber, waiting for the sovereign's ascent to the far shore. I request that his crime be investigated."
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Yan impeached him, saying, "Chen Jue remained at home, waiting for the emperor to die. I ask that his offense be investigated."

sentences.zh: 齊王不許。

translations.literal: The Prince of Qi did not permit it.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Qi refused.

sentences.zh: 自烈祖相吳，禁壓良為賤，令買奴婢者通官作券。

translations.literal: From the time the Founding Emperor served as chief minister of Wu, he forbade the forcing of free persons into servile status and ordered that those buying male and female slaves must register official certificates with the authorities.
translations.idiomatic: Ever since the Founding Emperor had served as chief minister of Wu, he had forbidden the press-ganging of free people into bondage and required all purchases of slaves to be recorded with official certificates.

sentences.zh: 馮延己及弟禮部員外郎延魯，俱在元帥府，草遺詔聽民賣男女；

translations.literal: Feng Yanji and his younger brother Yanlu, Outer Gentleman of the Ministry of Rites, were both in the commandery headquarters and drafted a testamentary edict permitting the people to sell sons and daughters;
translations.idiomatic: Feng Yanji and his younger brother Yanlu, an outer gentleman of the Ministry of Rites, both served in the prince's headquarters and drafted a testamentary edict allowing common people to sell their sons and daughters;

sentences.zh: 意欲自買姬妾，蕭儼駁曰：「此必延己等所為，非大行之命也。

translations.literal: their intent was to buy concubines for themselves. Xiao Yan rebutted, saying, "This must be the work of Yanji and the others; it is not the command of the late emperor.
translations.idiomatic: they intended to buy concubines for themselves. Xiao Yan objected: "This must be the work of Feng Yanji and his circle, not the late emperor's command.

sentences.zh: 昔延魯為東都判官，已有此請；

translations.literal: Formerly, when Yanlu was magistrate of the Eastern Capital, he had already made this request;
translations.idiomatic: When Yanlu had previously served as magistrate of the Eastern Capital, he had already made this same request;

sentences.zh: 先帝訪臣，臣對曰：『陛下昔為吳相，民有鬻男女者，為出府金，贖而歸之，故遠近歸心。

translations.literal: the late emperor questioned me, and I replied, 'Your Majesty, when you were formerly chief minister of Wu, whenever the people sold sons and daughters, you would disburse treasury gold to redeem them and send them home. Therefore near and far gave you their hearts.
translations.idiomatic: the late emperor consulted me, and I answered, 'When Your Majesty was chief minister of Wu, whenever people sold their children you paid out treasury funds to redeem them and send them home. That is why the realm rallied to you.

sentences.zh: 今即位而反之，使貧人之子為富人廝役，可乎？』

translations.literal: Now, upon ascending the throne, to reverse this and make the sons of the poor into menials for the rich—can that be permitted?'
translations.idiomatic: Now that you have taken the throne, to reverse that policy and turn the children of the poor into servants for the rich—can that be right?'

sentences.zh: 先帝以為然，將治延魯罪。

translations.literal: The late emperor thought this correct and was about to punish Yanlu for his crime.
translations.idiomatic: The late emperor agreed and was about to punish Yanlu.

sentences.zh: 臣以為延魯愚，無足責。

translations.literal: I considered Yanlu foolish and not worth blaming.
translations.idiomatic: I argued that Yanlu was merely foolish and not worth punishing.

sentences.zh: 先帝斜封延魯章，抹三筆，持入宮。

translations.literal: The late emperor sealed Yanlu's memorial askew, crossed out three strokes, and carried it into the palace.
translations.idiomatic: The late emperor sealed Yanlu's memorial askew, struck through three lines, and kept it in the palace.

sentences.zh: 請求諸宮中，必尚在。」

translations.literal: I request that it be sought among the palace records—it must still be there."
translations.idiomatic: Search the palace archives—it must still be there."

sentences.zh: 齊王命取先帝時留中章奏千餘道，皆斜封一抹，果得延魯疏。

translations.literal: The Prince of Qi ordered that more than a thousand memorials withheld during the late emperor's reign be retrieved—all sealed askew with a single stroke—and Yanlu's memorial was indeed found.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Qi ordered more than a thousand memorials withheld during the late emperor's reign to be brought out—all bearing the telltale diagonal seal—and Yanlu's memorial was found among them.

sentences.zh: 然以遺詔已行，竟不之改。

translations.literal: Yet because the testamentary edict had already been carried out, in the end it was not changed.
translations.idiomatic: But because the testamentary edict had already been promulgated, it was never revoked.

sentences.zh: 閩富沙王延政稱帝於建州，國號大殷，大赦，改元天德。

translations.literal: Yanzheng, Prince of Fusha in Min, declared himself emperor at Jian Prefecture. The state was named Great Yin. He granted a general amnesty and changed the era name to Tiande.
translations.idiomatic: Yanzheng, Prince of Fusha in Min, declared himself emperor at Jianzhou. He named his state Great Yin, proclaimed a general amnesty, and adopted the era name Tiande.

sentences.zh: 以將樂縣為鏞州，延平鎮為鐔州。

translations.literal: He made Jiangle County into Yong Prefecture and Yanping garrison into Tan Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He elevated Jiangle County to Yong Prefecture and Yanping garrison to Tan Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 立皇后張氏。

translations.literal: He installed Lady Zhang as empress.
translations.idiomatic: He made Lady Zhang his empress.

sentences.zh: 以節度判官潘承祐為吏部尚書，節度巡官建陽楊思恭為兵部尚書。

translations.literal: He appointed Pan Chengyou, judge of the military governorship, as Minister of Personnel, and Yang Sigong of Jianyang, touring official of the military governorship, as Minister of War.
translations.idiomatic: He appointed Pan Chengyou, judge of the military governorship, minister of personnel, and Yang Sigong of Jianyang, touring official of the military governorship, minister of war.

sentences.zh: 未幾，以承祐同平章事，思恭遷僕射，錄軍國事。

translations.literal: Before long, Chengyou was made co-director of the Secretariat, Sigong was promoted to Vice Director, and recorded military and state affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward Pan Chengyou was made co-director of the Secretariat, Yang Sigong was promoted to vice director, and both were charged with overseeing military and state affairs.

sentences.zh: 延政服赭袍視事，然牙參及接鄰國使者，猶如籓鎮禮。

translations.literal: Yanzheng wore a ochre robe when conducting affairs, yet in morning audience and when receiving envoys from neighboring states he still observed the protocol of a military governorship.
translations.idiomatic: Yanzheng wore an imperial ochre robe when holding court, yet in morning audience and when receiving envoys from neighboring states he still followed the etiquette of a vassal military governor.

sentences.zh: 殷國小民貧，軍旅不息。

translations.literal: The Yin state was small and its people poor; military campaigns never ceased.
translations.idiomatic: The Yin realm was small and its people poor, and warfare never ceased.

sentences.zh: 楊思恭以善聚斂得幸，增田畝山澤之稅，至於魚鹽蔬果，無不倍征，國人謂之「楊剝皮」。

translations.literal: Yang Sigong, through skill in gathering revenue, won favor. He increased taxes on fields, mountain lakes, and marshes; even fish, salt, fruit, and vegetables were all doubly levied. The people of the state called him "Yang the Skinner."
translations.idiomatic: Yang Sigong won favor through his talent for extracting revenue. He raised taxes on farmland, mountains, lakes, and marshes; even fish, salt, fruit, and vegetables were taxed at double rates. The people nicknamed him "Yang the Skinner."

sentences.zh: 三月，己卯朔，以中書令趙瑩為晉昌節度使兼中書令；

translations.literal: In the third month, on the first day jimao, Zhao Ying, Director of the Secretariat, was made Military Governor of Jinchang while retaining the title Director of the Secretariat;
translations.idiomatic: In the third month, on the first day jimao, Zhao Ying, director of the Secretariat, was appointed military governor of Jinchang while retaining his secretariat title;

sentences.zh: 以晉昌節度使兼侍中桑維翰為侍中。

translations.literal: Sang Weihan, Military Governor of Jinchang and Concurrent Palace Attendant, was made Palace Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: Sang Weihan, military governor of Jinchang and concurrent palace attendant, was confirmed as palace attendant.
