sentences.zh: 唐元宗即位，大赦，改元保大。

translations.literal: When Tang Yuanzong ascended the throne, he granted a general amnesty and changed the era name to Baoda.
translations.idiomatic: When Tang Yuanzong took the throne, he proclaimed a general amnesty and adopted the era name Baoda.

sentences.zh: 秘書郎韓熙載請俟逾年改元，不從。

translations.literal: Han Xizai, Secretary of the Secretariat, requested that the era name be changed only after the lapse of a year; this was not accepted.
translations.idiomatic: Han Xizai, a secretariat secretary, asked that the era name be changed only after a full year had passed, but the request was rejected.

sentences.zh: 尊皇后曰皇太后，立妃鍾氏為皇后。

translations.literal: The empress was honored as Empress Dowager, and Consort Zhong was installed as empress.
translations.idiomatic: The late emperor's consort was honored as empress dowager, and Lady Zhong was made empress.

sentences.zh: 唐主未聽政，馮延己屢入白事，一日至數四。

translations.literal: Before the Tang ruler began to hear cases, Feng Yanji repeatedly entered to report affairs—sometimes as many as four times in a single day.
translations.idiomatic: Before the new emperor began to hold audience, Feng Yanji repeatedly came to report business—sometimes as many as four times in one day.

sentences.zh: 唐主曰：「書記有常職，何為如是其煩也！」

translations.literal: The Tang ruler said, "The secretary has fixed duties—why are you so troublesome!"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "A secretary has defined duties. Why are you bothering me like this!"

sentences.zh: 唐主為人謙謹，初即位，不名大臣，數延公卿論政體，李建勳謂人曰：「主上寬仁大度，優於先帝；

translations.literal: The Tang ruler was by nature modest and cautious. When he first ascended the throne, he did not address ministers by name and repeatedly summoned high officials to discuss the form of government. Li Jianxun said to others, "The sovereign is generous and magnanimous, superior to the late emperor;
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was modest and careful by nature. When he first took the throne he did not address ministers by personal name and often summoned the high officials to discuss governance. Li Jianxun told others, "Our lord is generous and broad-minded, better than his father;

sentences.zh: 但性習未定，苟旁無正人，但恐不能守先帝之業耳。」

translations.literal: but his habits are not yet settled. If upright men are not at his side, I fear only that he may not be able to preserve the late emperor's enterprise.
translations.idiomatic: but his character is not yet fixed. Unless upright men stand beside him, I fear he may not be able to preserve what his father built.

sentences.zh: 唐主以鎮南節度使宋齊丘為太保兼中書令，奉化節度使周宗為侍中。

translations.literal: The Tang ruler made Song Qiqiu, Military Governor of Zhennan, Grand Mentor and Concurrent Director of the Secretariat, and Zhou Zong, Military Governor of Fenghua, Palace Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor appointed Song Qiqiu, military governor of Zhennan, grand mentor and concurrent director of the Secretariat, and Zhou Zong, military governor of Fenghua, palace attendant.

sentences.zh: 唐主以齊丘、宗先朝勳舊，故順人望召為相，政事皆自決之。

translations.literal: The Tang ruler, because Qiqiu and Zong were meritorious veterans of the previous reign, summoned them as chief ministers in accord with popular expectation, yet decided all affairs of government himself.
translations.idiomatic: Because Song Qiqiu and Zhou Zong were distinguished veterans of the previous reign, the emperor brought them into office as chief ministers to satisfy public expectation, but kept all major decisions in his own hands.

sentences.zh: 徙壽王景遂為燕王，宣城王景達為鄂王。

translations.literal: He transferred Prince Shou Jingsui to be Prince of Yan, and Prince Xuancheng Jingda to be Prince of E.
translations.idiomatic: He reassigned Prince Shou Jingsui as Prince of Yan and Prince Xuancheng Jingda as Prince of E.

sentences.zh: 初，唐主為齊王，知政事，每有過失，常夢錫常直言規正；

translations.literal: Earlier, when the Tang ruler was Prince of Qi and handled government affairs, whenever he committed an error Chang Mengxi would often speak bluntly to correct him;
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor had been Prince of Qi and handled government affairs, Chang Mengxi had often corrected him bluntly whenever he erred;

sentences.zh: 始雖忿懟，終以諒直多之。

translations.literal: at first he was angry and resentful, but in the end he valued Mengxi's straightforwardness.
translations.idiomatic: at first the prince resented it, but in time he came to value Mengxi's honesty.

sentences.zh: 及即位，許以為翰林學士，齊丘之黨疾之，坐封駁制書，貶池州判官。

translations.literal: When he ascended the throne, he had promised to appoint Mengxi Hanlin Academician, but Song Qiqiu's faction hated him. On the charge of sealing and rejecting an edict, he was demoted to magistrate of Chizhou.
translations.idiomatic: On taking the throne he had promised to make Chang Mengxi a hanlin academician, but Song Qiqiu's faction despised him. Mengxi was demoted to magistrate of Chizhou for having sealed and returned an edict.

sentences.zh: 池州多遷客，節度使上蔡王彥儔，防制過甚，幾不聊生，惟事夢錫如在朝廷。

translations.literal: Chizhou had many exiled officials. The Military Governor, Prince of Shangcai Yan Chou, guarded and restricted them excessively, so that they could scarcely live; only toward Mengxi did he treat affairs as though Mengxi were still at court.
translations.idiomatic: Chizhou held many exiled officials. Its military governor, Prince of Shangcai Yan Chou, restricted them so harshly that they could barely survive; only toward Chang Mengxi did he behave as though Mengxi were still at court.

sentences.zh: 宋齊丘待陳覺素厚，唐主亦以覺為有才，遂委任之。

translations.literal: Song Qiqiu had always treated Chen Jue with great favor, and the Tang ruler also considered Jue talented, so he entrusted him with office.
translations.idiomatic: Song Qiqiu had long favored Chen Jue, and the emperor also regarded him as talented, so he was given real authority.

sentences.zh: 馮延己、延魯、魏岑，雖齊邸舊僚，皆依附覺，與休寧查文徽更相汲引，侵蠹政事，唐人謂覺等為「五鬼」。

translations.literal: Feng Yanji, Yanlu, and Wei Cen, though old associates from the Prince of Qi's household, all attached themselves to Jue. Together with Zha Wenhu of Xiuning they mutually promoted one another, corrupting government affairs. The people of Tang called Jue and the others the "Five Demons."
translations.idiomatic: Feng Yanji, Yanlu, and Wei Cen, though old colleagues from the prince's household, all clustered around Chen Jue. With Zha Wenhu of Xiuning they promoted one another and preyed on the administration. The people of Tang called them the "Five Demons."

sentences.zh: 延魯自禮部員外郎遷中書舍人、勤政殿學士，江州觀察使杜昌業聞之，歎曰：「國家所以驅駕群臣，在官爵而已。

translations.literal: Yanlu was transferred from Outer Gentleman of the Ministry of Rites to Secretariat Drafter and Academician of the Hall of Diligent Governance. Du Changye, Observation Commissioner of Jiang Prefecture, heard of it and sighed, "The state drives its ministers by nothing but office and rank.
translations.idiomatic: Yanlu was promoted from outer gentleman of the Ministry of Rites to secretariat drafter and academician of the Hall of Diligent Governance. When Du Changye, observation commissioner of Jiangzhou, heard of it he sighed and said, "The state governs its ministers by office and rank alone.

sentences.zh: 若一言稱旨，遽躋通顯，後有立功者，何以賞之！」

translations.literal: If a single word pleases the sovereign and one immediately leaps to high prominence, then when others later achieve merit, by what means will they be rewarded!"
translations.idiomatic: If one pleasing word can vault a man straight to the highest honors, what reward will be left for those who actually perform meritorious service!"

sentences.zh: 未幾，唐主以岑及文徽皆為樞密副使。

translations.literal: Before long, the Tang ruler made both Cen and Wenhu Deputy Commissioners of the Bureau of Military Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Before long the emperor appointed both Wei Cen and Zha Wenhu deputy commissioners of the Bureau of Military Affairs.

sentences.zh: 岑既得志，會覺遭母喪，岑即暴揚覺過惡，擯斥之。

translations.literal: Once Cen had achieved his ambition, it happened that Jue was in mourning for his mother. Cen immediately exposed Jue's faults and drove him out.
translations.idiomatic: Once Wei Cen had gotten what he wanted, Chen Jue entered mourning for his mother. Cen immediately publicized Jue's misdeeds and had him expelled.

sentences.zh: 唐置定遠軍於濠州。

translations.literal: Tang established the Dingyuan Army at Hao Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Tang established the Dingyuan Army at Haozhou.

sentences.zh: 漢殤帝驕奢，不親政事。

translations.literal: Emperor Shang of Han was arrogant and extravagant and did not personally attend to government affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Shang of Later Han was arrogant and dissolute and neglected government.

sentences.zh: 高祖在殯，作樂酣飲；

translations.literal: While the Founding Emperor's coffin was still in the hall, he made music and drank deeply;
translations.idiomatic: Even while his father's coffin still lay in state, he ordered music and drank heavily;

sentences.zh: 夜與倡婦微行，裸男女而觀之。

translations.literal: at night he went out incognito with singing girls, stripping men and women naked to watch them.
translations.idiomatic: at night he slipped out incognito with singing girls and forced men and women to strip naked for his amusement.

sentences.zh: 左右忤意輒死，無敢諫者；

translations.literal: Those around him who displeased him were immediately put to death; none dared remonstrate;
translations.idiomatic: any attendant who displeased him was killed on the spot, and no one dared to remonstrate;

sentences.zh: 惟越王弘昌及內常侍番禺吳懷恩屢諫，不聽。

translations.literal: only the King of Yue, Hongchang, and the Inner Palace Attendant Wu Huai'en of Panyu repeatedly remonstrated, but he would not listen.
translations.idiomatic: only the King of Yue, Hongchang, and the inner palace attendant Wu Huai'en of Panyu repeatedly admonished him, but he refused to listen.

sentences.zh: 常猜忌諸弟，每宴集，令宦者守門，群臣、宗室，皆露索，然後入。

translations.literal: He often suspected his younger brothers. Whenever he held a banquet, he ordered eunuchs to guard the gate; ministers and members of the imperial clan all had to submit to a body search before entering.
translations.idiomatic: He constantly distrusted his younger brothers. At every banquet he posted eunuchs at the gates, and ministers and royal kinsmen were searched before they were allowed in.

sentences.zh: 晉王弘熙欲圖之，乃盛飾聲伎，娛悅其意，以成其惡。

translations.literal: The King of Jin, Hongxi, wished to plot against him, so he lavishly arrayed music and performers to please his mind and thereby complete his wickedness.
translations.idiomatic: The King of Jin, Hongxi, plotted to overthrow him and therefore lavished music and entertainers upon him, feeding his vices to bring about his downfall.

sentences.zh: 漢主好手搏，弘熙令指揮使陳道庠引力士劉思潮、譚令禋、林少強、林少良、何昌廷等五人習手搏於晉府，漢主聞而悅之。

translations.literal: The Han ruler loved hand-to-hand combat. Hongxi ordered the Commander Chen Daoxiang to bring the strongmen Liu Sichao, Tan Lingyin, Lin Shaoqiang, Lin Shaoliang, and He Changting—five men in all—to practice hand-to-hand combat at the Jin palace. The Han ruler heard of this and was pleased.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor loved wrestling. Hongxi had Commander Chen Daoxiang train five strongmen—Liu Sichao, Tan Lingyin, Lin Shaoqiang, Lin Shaoliang, and He Changting—in hand-to-hand combat at the Jin palace. The emperor heard of it and was delighted.

sentences.zh: 丙戌，與諸王宴於長春宮，觀手搏，至夕罷宴，漢主大醉。

translations.literal: On bingxu he banqueted with the princes at the Everlasting Spring Palace, watching hand-to-hand combat. The banquet lasted until evening and ended; the Han ruler was greatly drunk.
translations.idiomatic: On the day bingxu he feasted with the princes at Everlasting Spring Palace and watched the wrestling matches. The banquet ran until evening, and the emperor became thoroughly drunk.

sentences.zh: 弘熙使道庠、思潮等掖漢主，因拉殺之，盡殺其左右。

translations.literal: Hongxi had Daoxiang, Sichao, and the others support the Han ruler, then strangled him to death and killed all those around him.
translations.idiomatic: Hongxi had Chen Daoxiang, Liu Sichao, and the others support the emperor, then strangled him and killed all his attendants.

sentences.zh: 明旦，百官諸王莫敢入宮，越王弘昌帥諸弟臨於寢殿，迎弘熙即皇帝位，更名晟，改元應乾。

translations.literal: At dawn the next day, none of the officials or princes dared enter the palace. The King of Yue, Hongchang, led his younger brothers to the sleeping hall, welcomed Hongxi to the imperial throne, changed his name to Sheng, and changed the era name to Yingqian.
translations.idiomatic: The next morning no official or prince dared enter the palace. The King of Yue, Hongchang, led his brothers to the imperial bedchamber, installed Hongxi as emperor, changed his name to Sheng, and adopted the era name Yingqian.

sentences.zh: 以弘昌為太尉兼中書令、諸道兵馬都元帥，知政事，循王弘杲為副元帥，參預政事。

translations.literal: Hongchang was made Grand Marshal, Concurrent Director of the Secretariat, Commander-in-Chief of All Military Circuits, and Handler of Government Affairs; the King of Xun, Honggao, was made Deputy Commander-in-Chief and Participant in Government Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Hongchang was made grand marshal, concurrent director of the Secretariat, commander-in-chief of all military circuits, and head of government; the King of Xun, Honggao, was made deputy commander-in-chief with a seat in government.

sentences.zh: 陳道庠及劉思潮等皆受賞賜甚厚。

translations.literal: Chen Daoxiang and Liu Sichao and the others all received very rich rewards.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Daoxiang, Liu Sichao, and the others all received lavish rewards.

sentences.zh: 閩主曦納金吾使尚保殷之女，立為賢妃。

translations.literal: The ruler of Min, Xi, took as consort the daughter of the Commissioner of the Golden Guard, Shang Baoyin, and installed her as Worthy Consort.
translations.idiomatic: The ruler of Min, Xi, took the daughter of Golden Guard commissioner Shang Baoyin as consort and made her Worthy Consort.

sentences.zh: 妃有殊色，曦嬖之；

translations.literal: The consort had extraordinary beauty, and Xi favored her;
translations.idiomatic: The consort was exceptionally beautiful, and Xi doted on her;

sentences.zh: 醉中，妃所欲殺則殺之，所欲宥則宥之。

translations.literal: when drunk, whomever the consort wished killed, he killed; whomever she wished spared, he spared.
translations.idiomatic: when he was drunk, he executed whomever she wanted executed and pardoned whomever she wanted pardoned.

sentences.zh: 夏，四月，戊申朔，日有食之。

translations.literal: In summer, the fourth month, on the first day wushen, there was a solar eclipse.
translations.idiomatic: In summer, in the fourth month, on the first day wushen, the sun was eclipsed.

sentences.zh: 唐以中書侍郎、同平章事李建勳為昭武節度使，鎮撫州。

translations.literal: Tang made Li Jianxun, Vice Director of the Secretariat and Co-Director of the Secretariat, Military Governor of Zhaowu, stationed at Fu Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Tang appointed Li Jianxun, vice director and co-director of the Secretariat, military governor of Zhaowu, stationed at Fuzhou.

sentences.zh: 殷將陳望等攻閩福州，入其西郛，既而敗歸。

translations.literal: The Yin generals Chen Wang and others attacked Fuzhou in Min, entered its western outer wall, but afterward were defeated and returned.
translations.idiomatic: Yin generals including Chen Wang attacked Fuzhou in Min, broke into the western suburbs, but were eventually driven back in defeat.

sentences.zh: 五月，殷吏部尚書、同平章事潘承祐上書陳十事，大指言：「兄弟相攻，逆傷天理，一也。

translations.literal: In the fifth month, Pan Chengyou, Minister of Personnel and Co-Director of the Secretariat of Yin, submitted a memorial setting forth ten matters. The main points were: "Brothers attacking one another violates Heaven's principle—this is the first.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month, Pan Chengyou of Yin, minister of personnel and co-director of the Secretariat, submitted a memorial listing ten grievances. In essence he argued: "Brothers making war on one another violates Heaven's order—that is the first.

sentences.zh: 賦斂煩重，力役無節，二也。

translations.literal: Taxes and levies are burdensome and heavy; corvée labor is without restraint—this is the second.
translations.idiomatic: Taxes and levies are oppressive, and forced labor knows no limit—that is the second.

sentences.zh: 發民為兵，羈旅愁怨，三也。

translations.literal: Conscripting the people as soldiers—those far from home filled with sorrow and resentment; this is the third point.
translations.idiomatic: To conscript commoners into military service, leaving them far from home in sorrow and resentment—that is the third point.

sentences.zh: 楊思恭奪民衣食，使歸怨於上，群臣莫敢言，四也。

translations.literal: Yang Sigong seizing the people's food and clothing, causing resentment to be directed toward the ruler; among the ministers none dared speak—this is the fourth point.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Sigong confiscated the people's food and clothing and shifted the blame upward, so that resentment fell on the throne—yet none among the ministers dared speak out. That is the fourth point.

sentences.zh: 疆土狹隘，多置州縣，增吏困民，五也。

translations.literal: The territory narrow and cramped, yet many prefectures and counties were established, adding officials and burdening the people—this is the fifth point.
translations.idiomatic: Though the realm was small and cramped, the government multiplied prefectures and counties, piling on officials and grinding down the people. That is the fifth point.

sentences.zh: 除道裹糧，將攻臨汀，曾不憂金陵、錢塘乘虛相襲，六也。

translations.literal: Clearing roads and carrying provisions, intending to attack Linzhou, yet never worrying that Jinling and Qiantang might seize the opportunity and strike in turn—this is the sixth point.
translations.idiomatic: While clearing roads and packing supplies to attack Linzhou, there was no thought that Jinling and Qiantang might strike when the realm was exposed. That is the sixth point.

sentences.zh: 括高貲戶，財多者補官，逋負者被刑，七也。

translations.literal: Investigating wealthy households—those with great wealth were given official posts; those in arrears were punished—this is the seventh point.
translations.idiomatic: Rich households were shaken down: the wealthiest were bought off with official appointments, while those unable to pay were punished. That is the seventh point.

sentences.zh: 延平諸津，征果菜魚米，獲利至微，斂怨甚大，八也。

translations.literal: At the ferry points of Yanping, fruit, vegetables, fish, and grain were taxed; the profit was exceedingly small, yet the harvest of resentment was very great—this is the eighth point.
translations.idiomatic: At the Yanping ferry crossings, taxes were levied on fruit, vegetables, fish, and grain—petty gains that stirred deep resentment. That is the eighth point.

sentences.zh: 與唐、吳越為鄰，即位以來，未嘗通使，九也。

translations.literal: Bordering Tang and Wuyue, since ascending the throne, no envoys had ever been sent—this is the ninth point.
translations.idiomatic: Though neighbors to Tang and Wuyue, not once since accession had he exchanged envoys with them. That is the ninth point.

sentences.zh: 宮室台榭，崇飾無度，十也。」

translations.literal: Palaces, terraces, and pavilions—ornamented extravagantly without measure—this is the tenth point.
translations.idiomatic: Palaces, terraces, and pavilions were lavishly adorned beyond all limit. That is the tenth point.

sentences.zh: 殷王延政大怒，削承祐官爵，勒歸私第。

translations.literal: The Yin King, Yanzheng, was greatly enraged; he stripped Chengyou of his office and rank and ordered him to return to his private residence.
translations.idiomatic: Yinzheng was furious. He stripped Chengyou of rank and office and sent him home under restraint.

sentences.zh: 漢中宗既立，國中議論哅哅。

translations.literal: After Han Zhongzong was established on the throne, within the state discussion buzzed without end.
translations.idiomatic: Once Zhongzong of Han took the throne, the court buzzed with whisper and debate.

sentences.zh: 循王弘杲請斬劉思潮等以謝中外，漢主不從。

translations.literal: Prince Honggao of Xun requested that Liu Sichao and the others be executed to placate internal and external observers; the Han ruler did not consent.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Xun, Honggao, urged that Liu Sichao and his faction be put to death as a show of accountability at home and abroad. The Han sovereign refused.

sentences.zh: 思潮等聞之，譖弘杲謀反，漢主令思潮等伺之。

translations.literal: When Sichao and the others heard this, they slandered Honggao as plotting rebellion; the Han ruler ordered Sichao and the others to watch him.
translations.idiomatic: Sichao and his allies, hearing of it, accused Honggao of plotting rebellion. The Han ruler set them to spy on him.

sentences.zh: 弘杲方宴客，思潮與譚令禋帥衛兵突入，斬弘杲。

translations.literal: Honggao was just entertaining guests when Sichao, together with Tan Lingyin, led palace guards in a sudden entry and beheaded Honggao.
translations.idiomatic: Honggao was holding a banquet when Sichao and Tan Lingyin burst in at the head of the palace guard and cut him down.

sentences.zh: 於是漢主謀盡誅諸弟，以越王弘昌賢而得眾，尤忌之。

translations.literal: Thereupon the Han ruler plotted to execute all his brothers; because the Yue King, Hongchang, was virtuous and won the people's loyalty, he was especially feared.
translations.idiomatic: The Han ruler then resolved to destroy all his brothers. Prince Yue, Hongchang, won men's hearts by his virtue, and the sovereign feared him above all.

sentences.zh: 雄武節度使齊王弘弼，自以居大鎮，懼禍，求入朝；

translations.literal: Hongbi, Prince Qi and Military Commissioner of Xiongwu, thinking himself posted to a great commandery, feared disaster and requested permission to come to court;
translations.idiomatic: Prince Qi, Hongbi, Military Commissioner of Xiongwu, fearful that holding a major command made him a target, asked to be recalled to court;

sentences.zh: 許之。

translations.literal: Permission was granted.
translations.idiomatic: His request was granted.

sentences.zh: 初，閩主曦侍康宗宴，會新羅獻寶劍，康宗舉以示同平章事王倓曰：「此何所施？」

translations.literal: Formerly, when the Min ruler Xi attended a banquet with Kangzong, it happened that Silla presented a treasured sword; Kangzong raised it to show Associate Grand Councillor Wang Tan and said: "For what is this used?"
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, while the Min ruler Xi was attending a feast with Kangzong, Silla presented a precious sword. Kangzong lifted it and showed it to Wang Tan, Associate Grand Councillor, asking, "What is this for?"

sentences.zh: 倓對曰：「斬為臣不忠者。」

translations.literal: Tan replied: "To behead disloyal ministers."
translations.idiomatic: Tan answered, "To behead ministers who are disloyal."

sentences.zh: 時曦己蓄異志，凜然變色。

translations.literal: At that time Xi had already harbored divergent intentions and changed color with a chill severity.
translations.idiomatic: Xi already nursed secret ambitions, and his face turned pale.

sentences.zh: 至是宴群臣，復有獻劍者，曦命發校塚，斬其屍。

translations.literal: At this time, when feasting with the ministers, there was again one who presented a sword; Xi ordered Wang's tomb opened and his corpse beheaded.
translations.idiomatic: Now, at a banquet with his ministers, another sword was presented. Xi had Wang's grave opened and his corpse beheaded.

sentences.zh: 校書郎陳光逸謂其友曰：「主上失德，亡無日矣，吾欲死諫。」

translations.literal: Proofreader Chen Guangyi said to his friend: "The sovereign has lost virtue; destruction is not many days away. I wish to remonstrate unto death."
translations.idiomatic: Chen Guangyi, a proofreader, told a friend, "The sovereign has lost the Way. His fall cannot be far off. I mean to remonstrate with my life."

sentences.zh: 其友止之，不從；

translations.literal: His friend tried to stop him; he would not listen;
translations.idiomatic: His friend tried to hold him back, but he would not be dissuaded;

sentences.zh: 上書陳曦大惡五十事。

translations.literal: He submitted a memorial laying out fifty great evils of Xi.
translations.idiomatic: He submitted a memorial enumerating fifty grievous crimes of Xi's reign.

sentences.zh: 曦怒，命衛士鞭之數百，不死；

translations.literal: Xi was enraged and ordered the guards to lash him hundreds of times; he did not die;
translations.idiomatic: Xi had his guards whip him hundreds of times; still he would not die;

sentences.zh: 以繩系其頸，懸諸庭樹，久之乃絕。

translations.literal: A rope was tied around his neck and he was hung from a tree in the courtyard; only after a long while did he expire.
translations.idiomatic: They bound a rope around his neck and hung him from a tree in the courtyard. A long while passed before he finally died.

sentences.zh: 秋，七月，己丑，詔以年饑，國用不足，分遣使者六十餘人於諸道括民谷。

translations.literal: In autumn, the seventh month, on jichou, an edict was issued: because of famine that year and insufficient state revenue, more than sixty envoys were dispatched to the various circuits to requisition the people's grain.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of autumn, on jichou, an edict went forth: famine had emptied the treasury, so more than sixty envoys were sent through every circuit to seize grain from the people.

sentences.zh: 吳越王弘佐初立，上統軍使闞璠強戾，排斥異己，弘佐不能制；

translations.literal: When Wuyue King Hongzuo first acceded, Senior Commanding General Kan Fan was fierce and obstinate, driving out those unlike himself, and Hongzuo could not control him;
translations.idiomatic: When King Hongzuo of Wuyue first took the throne, Senior Commanding General Kan Fan ruled by force, purging rivals, and the young king could not rein him in;

sentences.zh: 內牙上都監使章德安數與之爭，右都監使李文慶不附於璠，乙巳，貶德安於處州，文慶於睦州。

translations.literal: Chief Palace Guard Supervisor Zhang De'an frequently quarreled with him; Right Chief Supervisor Li Wenqing would not attach himself to Fan; on yisi, De'an was demoted to Chuzhou, Wenqing to Muzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Chief Palace Guard Supervisor Zhang De'an clashed with Fan repeatedly; Right Chief Supervisor Li Wenqing refused to follow him. On yisi, De'an was banished to Chuzhou and Wenqing to Muzhou.

sentences.zh: 璠與右統軍使胡進思益專橫。

translations.literal: Fan and Right Commanding General Hu Jinsi grew all the more domineering.
translations.idiomatic: Fan and Right Commanding General Hu Jinsi grew only more overbearing.

sentences.zh: 璠，明州人；

translations.literal: Fan was a native of Mingzhou;
translations.idiomatic: Fan was from Mingzhou;

sentences.zh: 文慶，睦州人；

translations.literal: Wenqing was a native of Muzhou;
translations.idiomatic: Wenqing was from Muzhou;

sentences.zh: 進思，湖州人也。

translations.literal: Jinsi was a native of Huzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Jinsi was from Huzhou.

sentences.zh: 唐主緣烈祖意，以天雄節度使兼中書令、金陵尹燕王景遂為諸道兵馬元帥，徙封齊王，居東宮；

translations.literal: Following the late founder's intent, the Tang ruler appointed Prince Jingsui of Yan—Military Commissioner of Tianxiong, concurrent Grand Council Prefect, and Prefect of Jinling—as Commander-in-Chief of all forces; his title was changed to Prince Qi and he was installed in the Eastern Palace;
translations.idiomatic: Honoring his grandfather the Founder's wishes, the Tang sovereign named Prince Jingsui of Yan—Military Commissioner of Tianxiong, concurrent Chief Councillor, and Prefect of Jinling—Commander-in-Chief of all armies, transferred his title to Prince Qi, and installed him in the Eastern Palace;

sentences.zh: 天平節度使、守侍中、東都留守鄂王景達為副元帥，徙封燕王；

translations.literal: Prince Jingda of E—Military Commissioner of Tianping, Acting Chief Councillor, and Eastern Capital Regent—was made Deputy Commander-in-Chief, and his title was changed to Prince Yan;
translations.idiomatic: Prince Jingda of E, Military Commissioner of Tianping, Acting Chief Councillor, and Eastern Capital Regent, was made Deputy Commander-in-Chief and given the title Prince of Yan;

sentences.zh: 宣告中外，約以傳位。

translations.literal: This was proclaimed within and without, with a pledge that the throne would pass accordingly.
translations.idiomatic: The court announced it at home and abroad, binding itself to pass the succession as promised.

sentences.zh: 立長子弘冀為南昌王。

translations.literal: The eldest son Hongji was established as Prince of Nanchang.
translations.idiomatic: He made his eldest son, Hongji, Prince of Nanchang.

sentences.zh: 景遂、景達固辭，不許。

translations.literal: Jingsui and Jingda firmly declined; permission was not granted.
translations.idiomatic: Jingsui and Jingda protested again and again, but the sovereign would not relent.

sentences.zh: 景遂自誓必不敢為嗣，更其字曰退身。

translations.literal: Jingsui vowed by himself that he would never dare to become heir, and changed his style name to Tuishen ("Withdraw from the Body").
translations.idiomatic: Jingsui swore he would never accept the succession and changed his style name to Tuishen—"Withdrawing from Office."

sentences.zh: 漢指揮使萬景忻敗張遇賢於循州。

translations.literal: Han Commanding General Wan Jingxin defeated Zhang Yuxian at Xunzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Wan Jingxin, a Han commanding general, defeated Zhang Yuxian at Xunzhou.

sentences.zh: 遇賢告於神，神曰：「取虔州，則大事可成。」

translations.literal: Yuxian appealed to the spirit, and the spirit said: "Take Qianzhou, and the great undertaking can succeed."
translations.idiomatic: Yuxian prayed to a god, and the god answered, "Seize Qianzhou, and your great cause will succeed."

sentences.zh: 遇賢帥眾逾嶺，趣虔州。

translations.literal: Yuxian led the multitude over the mountains and hastened toward Qianzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Yuxian led his host across the mountains toward Qianzhou.

sentences.zh: 唐百勝節度使賈匡浩不為備，遇賢眾十餘萬攻陷諸縣，再敗州兵，城門晝閉。

translations.literal: Tang Military Commissioner Jia Kuanghao of Baisheng made no preparations; Yuxian's force of more than a hundred thousand seized the various counties, twice defeated the prefectural troops, and the city gates were closed even by day.
translations.idiomatic: Jia Kuanghao, Tang Military Commissioner of Baisheng, was caught unprepared. Yuxian's army of more than a hundred thousand overran the counties, twice routed the prefectural forces, and by daylight the city gates had to be shut.

sentences.zh: 遇賢作宮室營署於白雲洞，遣將四出剽掠。

translations.literal: Yuxian built palaces and government offices at Baiyun Cave and dispatched generals in all directions to plunder.
translations.idiomatic: Yuxian built palaces and camps at Baiyun Cave and sent generals out on every side to pillage.

sentences.zh: 匡浩，公鐸之子也。

translations.literal: Kuanghao was the son of Gongduo.
translations.idiomatic: Kuanghao was Gongduo's son.

sentences.zh: 八月，乙卯，唐主立弟景逷為保寧王。

translations.literal: In the eighth month, on yimao, the Tang ruler established his younger brother Jingyao as Prince of Baoning.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month, on yimao, the Tang sovereign ennobled his younger brother Jingyao as Prince of Baoning.

sentences.zh: 宋太后怨种夫人，屢欲害景逷，唐主力保全之。

translations.literal: Empress Dowager Song resented Lady Zhong and repeatedly sought to harm Jingyao; the Tang ruler exerted himself to protect him.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Dowager Song hated Lady Zhong and more than once tried to destroy Jingyao. The Tang sovereign shielded him with all his power.

sentences.zh: 夏州牙內指揮使拓跋崇斌謀作亂，綏州刺史李彝敏將助之，事覺；

translations.literal: Tuo Ba Chongbin, Internal Commanding General of Xiazhou's guard, plotted rebellion; Prefect of Suizhou Li Yimin was about to assist him; the affair was discovered;
translations.idiomatic: Tuoba Chongbin, an internal commanding general of the Xiazhou guard, plotted rebellion, and Li Yimin, prefect of Suizhou, meant to join him. The plot was uncovered;

sentences.zh: 辛未，彝敏棄州，與其弟彝俊等五人奔延州。

translations.literal: On xinwei, Yimin abandoned the prefecture and, with his younger brother Yijun and four others—five in all—fled to Yanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: On xinwei, Yimin abandoned his post and fled to Yanzhou with his brother Yijun and three others—five men in all.

sentences.zh: 九月，尊帝母秦國夫人安氏為皇太妃。

translations.literal: In the ninth month, the emperor's mother, Lady An of Qin State, was honored as Imperial Grand Consort.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month, the emperor's mother, Lady An of Qin, was raised to the rank of Imperial Grand Consort.

sentences.zh: 妃，代北人也。

translations.literal: The Grand Consort was a native of northern Dai.
translations.idiomatic: She came from the northern Dai region.

sentences.zh: 帝事太后、太妃甚謹，多侍食於其宮，待諸弟亦友愛。

translations.literal: The emperor served the empress dowager and the grand consort with great reverence, often dining in their palaces; he also treated his younger brothers with fraternal affection.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor tended the empress dowager and the grand consort with scrupulous devotion, often taking his meals in their quarters, and treated his younger brothers with genuine warmth.

sentences.zh: 初，河陽牙將喬榮從趙延壽入契丹，契丹以為回圖使，往來販易於晉，置邸大梁。

translations.literal: Formerly, Hegang guard officer Qiao Rong followed Zhao Yanshou into Khitan territory; the Khitan appointed him emissary for return trade, traveling back and forth to trade with Jin and establishing a residence in Daliang.
translations.idiomatic: In earlier days, Qiao Rong, a guard officer at Heyang, had followed Zhao Yanshou into Khitan lands. The Khitan made him their trade envoy to Jin and set up a merchant house for him at Daliang.

sentences.zh: 及契丹與晉有隙，景延廣說帝囚榮於獄，悉取邸中之貨。

translations.literal: When rift arose between Khitan and Jin, Jing Yanguang persuaded the emperor to imprison Rong and seize all the goods in his residence.
translations.idiomatic: When relations between Khitan and Jin soured, Jing Yanguang urged the emperor to throw Rong in prison and confiscate everything in his depot.

sentences.zh: 凡契丹之人販易在晉境者，皆殺之，奪其貨。

translations.literal: All Khitan persons trading within Jin territory were killed and their goods seized.
translations.idiomatic: Every Khitan trader found within Jin borders was killed and plundered.

sentences.zh: 大臣皆言契丹有大功於晉，不可負。

translations.literal: The great ministers all said the Khitan had rendered great service to Jin and must not be wronged.
translations.idiomatic: The senior ministers all protested that the Khitan had done Jin great service and must not be betrayed.

sentences.zh: 戊子，釋榮，慰賜而歸之。

translations.literal: On wuzi, Rong was released, consoled and rewarded, and sent home.
translations.idiomatic: On wuzi, Rong was freed, soothed with gifts, and sent back.

sentences.zh: 榮辭延廣，延廣大言曰：「歸語而主，先帝為北朝所立，故稱臣奉表。

translations.literal: As Rong took leave of Yanguang, Yanguang spoke grandly: "Return and tell your lord: the late emperor was enthroned by the Northern Court, hence he styled himself subject and sent tribute.
translations.idiomatic: When Rong came to say farewell, Yanguang thundered, "Go tell your master: our late emperor was placed on the throne by the Northern Court, so he called himself subject and sent tribute.

sentences.zh: 今上乃中國所立，所以降志於北朝者，正以不敢忘先帝盟約故耳。

translations.literal: The present emperor was enthroned by China itself; the reason he lowered his ambitions toward the Northern Court is simply that he dared not forget the late emperor's covenant.
translations.idiomatic: The present emperor was raised by the Middle Kingdom itself. He abases himself before the Northern Court only because he dares not forget our late sovereign's sworn pact.

sentences.zh: 為鄰稱孫，足矣，無稱臣之理。

translations.literal: As a neighbor to call oneself grandson is already enough; there is no reason to call oneself subject.
translations.idiomatic: As neighbors go, calling yourself grandson is enough. There is no call to play the subject.

sentences.zh: 北朝皇帝勿信趙延壽誑誘，輕侮中國。

translations.literal: The Northern Court emperor must not believe Zhao Yanshou's deception and contemn China.
translations.idiomatic: Let the Khitan emperor not trust Zhao Yanshou's poison or hold the Middle Kingdom in contempt.

sentences.zh: 中國士馬，爾所目睹。

translations.literal: China's officers and horses—you have seen them with your own eyes.
translations.idiomatic: You have seen our soldiers and horses with your own eyes.

sentences.zh: 翁怒則來戰，孫有十萬橫磨劍，足以相待。

translations.literal: When the old man is angry, let him come to battle; this grandson has a hundred thousand swords whetted on the whetstone, enough to answer the challenge.
translations.idiomatic: If the old man wants war, let him bring it. Your grandson keeps a hundred thousand swords whetted on the whetstone, enough to meet him.

sentences.zh: 它日為孫所敗，取笑天下，毋悔也！」

translations.literal: If another day you are defeated by this grandson and become the laughingstock of all under Heaven—do not regret it!
translations.idiomatic: When my grandson beats you someday and all the world laughs, do not say you were not warned!

sentences.zh: 榮自以亡失貨財，恐歸獲罪，且欲為異時據驗，乃曰：「公所言頗多，懼有遺忘，願記之紙墨。」

translations.literal: Rong, thinking he had lost his goods and fearing punishment on return, and also wishing to have proof for another day, said: "Sir, you have spoken at great length; I fear I may forget; I beg that it be written on paper."
translations.idiomatic: Rong, having lost his property and fearing punishment at home—and wanting proof for later—said, "You have said a great deal, sir. I am afraid I may forget. Would you put it in writing?"

sentences.zh: 延廣命吏書其語以授之，榮具以白契丹主。

translations.literal: Yanguang ordered a clerk to write down his words and give them to him; Rong reported everything in full to the Khitan ruler.
translations.idiomatic: Yanguang had a clerk write down every word and hand the record to Rong, who carried the whole account to the Khitan sovereign.

sentences.zh: 契丹主大怒，入寇之志始決。

translations.literal: The Khitan ruler was greatly enraged, and his resolve to invade was at last set.
translations.idiomatic: The Khitan sovereign flew into a rage, and from that moment his mind was set on invasion.

sentences.zh: 晉使如契丹，皆縶之幽州，不得見。

translations.literal: Jin envoys sent to Khitan were all detained at Youzhou and not permitted audience.
translations.idiomatic: Every Jin envoy sent to Khitan was held at Youzhou and denied an audience.

sentences.zh: 桑維翰屢請遜辭以謝契丹，每為延廣所沮。

translations.literal: Sang Weihan repeatedly requested humble language to apologize to Khitan, but each time was thwarted by Yanguang.
translations.idiomatic: Sang Weihan pleaded again and again for conciliatory language toward Khitan, and each time Yanguang blocked him.

sentences.zh: 帝以延廣為有定策功，故寵冠群臣；

translations.literal: The emperor, because Yanguang had merit in settling the succession, favored him above all ministers;
translations.idiomatic: Because Yanguang had helped settle the succession, the emperor favored him above every other minister;

sentences.zh: 又總宿衛兵，故大臣莫能與之爭。

translations.literal: He also commanded the palace guard troops, so the great ministers could not contend with him.
translations.idiomatic: and he commanded the palace guard besides, so no senior minister could stand against him.

sentences.zh: 河東節度使劉知遠，知延廣必致寇，而畏其方用事，不敢言，但益募兵，奏置興捷、武節等十餘軍以備契丹。

translations.literal: Liu Zhiyuan, Military Commissioner of Hedong, knew Yanguang would surely bring invasion, yet feared his present grip on power and dared not speak; he only increased recruitment and memorialized to establish more than ten armies such as Xingjie and Wujie to prepare against Khitan.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Zhiyuan of Hedong saw that Yanguang would bring the Khitan down on them, but Yanguang was in the ascendant and Liu dared not speak. He raised troops in secret and petitioned to form more than a dozen new armies—Xingjie, Wujie, and the rest—to hold Khitan at bay.

sentences.zh: 甲午，定難節度使李彝殷奏李彝敏作亂之狀，詔執彝敏送夏州，斬之。

translations.literal: On jiawu, Li Yiyin, Military Commissioner of Dingnan, memorialized the circumstances of Li Yimin's rebellion; an edict ordered Yimin seized and sent to Xiazhou, where he was executed.
translations.idiomatic: On jiawu, Li Yiyin, Military Commissioner of Dingnan, reported Li Yimin's rebellion. An edict ordered Yimin seized, sent to Xiazhou, and executed.

sentences.zh: 冬，十月，戊申，立吳國夫人馮氏為皇后。

translations.literal: In winter, the tenth month, on wushen, Lady Feng of Wu State was established as empress.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month of winter, on wushen, Lady Feng of Wu was crowned empress.

sentences.zh: 初，高祖愛少弟重胤，養以為子；

translations.literal: Formerly, Gaozu loved his youngest brother Chongyin and adopted him as a son;
translations.idiomatic: Long ago, Gaozu had doted on his youngest brother Chongyin and raised him as a son;

sentences.zh: 及留守鄴都，娶副留守安喜馮濛女為其婦。

translations.literal: When garrisoning Ye, he took as wife for him the daughter of Deputy Regent Feng Meng of Anxi.
translations.idiomatic: While stationed at Ye, he had married him to Feng Meng of Anxi's daughter, the deputy regent's child.

sentences.zh: 重胤早卒，馮夫人寡居，有美色，帝見而悅之；

translations.literal: Chongyin died young; Lady Feng lived as a widow and was beautiful; the emperor saw her and was pleased;
translations.idiomatic: Chongyin died young. Lady Feng, widowed and beautiful, caught the emperor's eye;

sentences.zh: 高祖崩，梓宮在殯，帝遂納之。

translations.literal: When Gaozu died, with the coffin still in mourning hall, the emperor then took her in marriage.
translations.idiomatic: and the moment Gaozu died, with the imperial coffin still in state, the new emperor took her for his own.

sentences.zh: 群臣皆賀，帝謂馮道等曰：「皇太后之命，與卿等不任大慶。」

translations.literal: The ministers all offered congratulations; the emperor said to Feng Dao and the others: "By the empress dowager's command, I am unable to hold a great celebration with you."
translations.idiomatic: The court offered congratulations. The emperor told Feng Dao and the rest, "By the empress dowager's command, I cannot hold a grand celebration with you."

sentences.zh: 群臣出，帝與夫人酣飲，過梓宮前，醊而告曰：「皇太后之命，與先帝不任大慶。」

translations.literal: When the ministers had departed, the emperor drank deeply with the lady; passing before the coffin, he poured libation and announced: "By the empress dowager's command, I am unable to hold a great celebration with the late emperor."
translations.idiomatic: After the ministers left, he drank deep with his new consort. Passing the coffin, he poured a libation and said, "By the empress dowager's command, the late emperor and I cannot share in any grand rejoicing."

sentences.zh: 左右失笑，帝亦自笑，顧謂左右曰：「我今日作新婿，何如？」

translations.literal: Those around him could not help laughing; the emperor laughed too, turned to those beside him and said: "How do I look as a new bridegroom today?"
translations.idiomatic: His attendants burst out laughing. The emperor laughed too, turned to them and asked, "How do I look as a bridegroom today?"

sentences.zh: 夫人與左右皆大笑。

translations.literal: The lady and those around all laughed loudly.
translations.idiomatic: The lady and the attendants roared with laughter.

sentences.zh: 太后雖恚，而無如之何。

translations.literal: Though the empress dowager was furious, she could do nothing about it.
translations.idiomatic: The empress dowager was furious, but there was nothing she could do.

sentences.zh: 既正位中宮，頗預政事。

translations.literal: Once installed in the central palace as empress, she took part in government affairs to a considerable degree.
translations.idiomatic: Once enthroned as empress, she began to dabble in state affairs.

sentences.zh: 後兄玉，時為禮部郎中、鹽鐵判官，帝驟擢用至端明殿學士、戶部侍郎，與議政事。

translations.literal: Her elder brother Yu, then a Director in the Ministry of Rites and Salt and Iron Commissioner, was abruptly promoted to Academician of the Hall of Brilliant Governance and Vice Minister of Revenue, and participated in deliberating government affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Her elder brother Yu, then a director in the Ministry of Rites and salt-and-iron commissioner, was catapulted to Academician of the Hall of Brilliant Governance and Vice Minister of Revenue, and given a seat in policy debates.

sentences.zh: 漢主命韶王弘雅致仕。

translations.literal: The Han ruler ordered Prince Hongya of Shao to resign from office.
translations.idiomatic: The Han sovereign ordered Prince Shao, Hongya, to retire from office.

sentences.zh: 唐主遣洪州營屯都虞候嚴恩將兵討張遇賢，以通事舍人金陵邊鎬為監軍。

translations.literal: The Tang ruler dispatched Yan En, Chief Adjutant of Hongzhou's Garrison Farming Corps, to lead troops against Zhang Yuxian, with Jinling native Bian Hao, Protocol Officer, as army inspector.
translations.idiomatic: The Tang sovereign sent Yan En, chief adjutant of Hongzhou's garrison farms, to campaign against Zhang Yuxian, with Bian Hao of Jinling—a protocol officer—as military inspector.

sentences.zh: 鎬用虞州人白昌裕為謀主，擊張遇賢；

translations.literal: Hao employed Bai Changyu of Yuzhou as his chief strategist and struck at Zhang Yuxian;
translations.idiomatic: Hao put Bai Changyu of Yuzhou in charge of strategy and attacked Zhang Yuxian;

sentences.zh: 屢破之。

translations.literal: repeatedly defeating him.
translations.idiomatic: breaking him again and again.

sentences.zh: 遇賢禱於神，神不復言，其徒大懼。

translations.literal: Yuxian prayed to the spirit; the spirit no longer spoke; his followers were greatly terrified.
translations.idiomatic: Yuxian prayed to his god, but the god fell silent. His followers were seized with terror.

sentences.zh: 昌裕勸鎬伐木開道，出其營後襲之，遇賢棄眾奔別將李台。

translations.literal: Changyu urged Hao to cut trees and open a path, coming out behind the camp to strike; Yuxian abandoned his force and fled to Deputy General Li Tai.
translations.idiomatic: Changyu told Hao to cut a road through the forest and fall on the rebel camp from behind. Yuxian abandoned his army and fled to the deputy commander Li Tai.

sentences.zh: 台知神無驗，執遇賢以降，斬於金陵市。

translations.literal: Tai, knowing the spirit had no efficacy, seized Yuxian and surrendered; he was beheaded in the Jinling marketplace.
translations.idiomatic: Li Tai, seeing the god had failed, seized Yuxian and surrendered. Yuxian was beheaded in the Jinling market.

sentences.zh: 十一月，丁亥，漢主祀南郊，大赦，改元乾和。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month, on dinghai, the Han ruler sacrificed at the southern suburb, proclaimed a general amnesty, and changed the era name to Qianhe.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month, on dinghai, the Han sovereign sacrificed at the southern altar, proclaimed a general amnesty, and adopted the era name Qianhe.

sentences.zh: 戊子，吳越王弘佐納妃仰氏，仁詮之女也。

translations.literal: On wuzi, Wuyue King Hongzuo took as consort Lady Yang, daughter of Renquan.
translations.idiomatic: On wuzi, King Hongzuo of Wuyue took Lady Yang, Renquan's daughter, as consort.

sentences.zh: 初，高祖以馬三百借平盧節度使楊光遠，景延廣以詔命取之。

translations.literal: Formerly, Gaozu had lent three hundred horses to Yang Guangyuan, Military Commissioner of Pinglu; Jing Yanguang by imperial decree took them back.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Gaozu had lent three hundred horses to Yang Guangyuan, Military Commissioner of Pinglu. Jing Yanguang now reclaimed them by imperial order.

sentences.zh: 光遠怒曰：「是疑我也。」

translations.literal: Guangyuan said angrily: "This means they suspect me."
translations.idiomatic: Guangyuan raged, "They mean to suspect me."

sentences.zh: 密召其子單州刺史承祚，戊戌，承祚稱母病，夜，開門奔青州。

translations.literal: Secretly he summoned his son Chengzhu, Prefect of Shanzhou; on wuxu, Chengzhu claimed his mother was ill; that night he opened the gates and fled to Qingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He secretly summoned his son Chengzhu, prefect of Shanzhou. On wuxu, Chengzhu feigned his mother's illness; that night he threw open the gates and fled to Qingzhou.

sentences.zh: 庚子，以左飛龍使金城何超權知單州。

translations.literal: On gengzi, Left Flying Dragon Commissioner Jin Cheng He Chao was appointed acting Prefect of Shanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: On gengzi, Left Flying Dragon Commissioner He Chao of Jincheng was made acting prefect of Shanzhou.

sentences.zh: 遣內班賜光遠玉帶、御馬、金帛，以安其意。

translations.literal: Palace attendants were dispatched to bestow upon Guangyuan a jade belt, imperial horses, gold, and silk, to soothe his mind.
translations.idiomatic: The court sent palace attendants with a jade belt, an imperial horse, gold, and silk to reassure Guangyuan.

sentences.zh: 壬寅，遣侍衛步軍都指揮使郭謹將兵戍鄆州。

translations.literal: On renyin, Palace Guard Infantry Commander Guo Jin was dispatched to lead troops to garrison Yanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: On renyin, Palace Guard Infantry Commander Guo Jin was sent to garrison Yanzhou with his troops.

sentences.zh: 唐葬光文肅武孝高皇帝於永陵，唐號烈祖。

translations.literal: Tang buried the emperor Guangwensu Wu Xiaogao at Yongling; Tang posthumously styled him Liezu (Grand Founder).
translations.idiomatic: Tang interred Emperor Guangwensu Wu Xiaogao at Yongling and gave him the temple name Liezu, the Grand Founder.

sentences.zh: 十二月，乙巳朔，遣左領軍衛將軍蔡行遇將兵戍鄆州。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month, on the yisi new moon, the Left Leader of the Imperial Guard General Cai Xingyu was dispatched to lead troops to garrison Yan Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month, on the yisi new moon, General Cai Xingyu of the Left Imperial Guard was sent to Yanzhou with troops to take up the garrison.

sentences.zh: 楊光遠遣騎兵入淄州，劫刺史翟進宗歸於青州。

translations.literal: Yang Guangyuan sent cavalry into Zi Prefecture, seized the prefect Zhai Jinzong, and took him back to Qing Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Guangyuan sent cavalry into Zizhou, abducted Prefect Zhai Jinzong, and carried him off to Qingzhou.

sentences.zh: 甲寅，徙楊承祚為登州刺史以從其便。

translations.literal: On jiayin, Yang Chengzuo was transferred to be prefect of Deng Prefecture so as to suit his convenience.
translations.idiomatic: On jiayin, Yang Chengzuo was reassigned as prefect of Dengzhou at his own request.

sentences.zh: 光遠益驕，密告契丹，以晉主負德違盟，境內大饑，公私困竭，乘此際攻之，一舉可取；

translations.literal: Guangyuan grew ever more arrogant and secretly informed the Khitan that the Jin ruler had failed in virtue and broken the alliance, that famine was severe within the realm, and that public and private resources were exhausted — if they attacked at this moment, they could take it in one stroke;
translations.idiomatic: Yang Guangyuan grew ever bolder and secretly urged the Khitan: the Jin emperor had betrayed the alliance, famine ravaged the realm, and public coffers were empty — strike now and the conquest would be won in a single blow;

sentences.zh: 趙延壽亦勸之。

translations.literal: Zhao Yanshou also urged this.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Yanshou seconded the advice.

sentences.zh: 契丹主乃集山後及盧龍兵合五萬人，使延壽將之，委延壽經略中國，曰：「若得之，當立汝為帝。」

translations.literal: The Khitan ruler thereupon assembled troops from the lands beyond the mountains and from Lulong, totaling fifty thousand men, and had Yanshou command them. He entrusted Yanshou with planning the conquest of China, saying: "If we take it, I shall install you as emperor."
translations.idiomatic: The Khitan khagan mustered fifty thousand men from the lands beyond the mountains and from Lulong and placed them under Yanshou's command. He entrusted the China campaign to Yanshou, saying: "If we win, I shall make you emperor."

sentences.zh: 又常指延壽謂晉人曰：「此汝主也。」

translations.literal: He also often pointed at Yanshou and said to the Jin people: "This is your lord."
translations.idiomatic: He would often point at Yanshou and tell Jin subjects: "This man is your sovereign."

sentences.zh: 延壽信之，由是為契丹盡力，畫取中國之策。

translations.literal: Yanshou believed this, and from then on exerted himself fully for the Khitan, devising strategies to seize China.
translations.idiomatic: Yanshou took him at his word and from then on threw himself into the Khitan cause, drafting plan after plan for the conquest of China.

sentences.zh: 朝廷頗聞其謀，丙辰，遣使城南樂及德清軍，征近道兵以備之。

translations.literal: The court heard much of this plot. On bingchen, envoys were dispatched to the southern garrisons at Yue and Deqing to levy nearby troops in preparation.
translations.idiomatic: Word of the plot reached the court. On bingchen, envoys were sent to the southern garrisons at Yue and Deqing to raise local troops in readiness.

sentences.zh: 唐侍中周宗年老，恭謹自守，中書令宋齊丘廣樹朋黨，百計傾之。

translations.literal: Tang's Vice Grand Councilor Zhou Zong was advanced in years, reverent and cautious in self-restraint. The Chief Councilor Song Qiqiu widely cultivated a faction and by a hundred schemes sought to overthrow him.
translations.idiomatic: Tang Vice Grand Councilor Zhou Zong was elderly, reverent, and self-restrained. Chief Councilor Song Qiqiu built a wide patronage network and schemed by every means to bring him down.

sentences.zh: 宗泣訴於唐王，唐主由是薄齊丘。

translations.literal: Zong wept and appealed to the Tang ruler; the Tang lord thereupon came to think less of Qiqiu.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Zong wept before the Tang emperor and pleaded his case; from that point the emperor's regard for Song Qiqiu cooled.

sentences.zh: 既而陳覺被疏，乃出齊丘為鎮海節度使。

translations.literal: Soon afterward, when Chen Jue fell out of favor, Qiqiu was sent out to serve as military governor of Zhenhai.
translations.idiomatic: When Chen Jue later fell from favor, Song Qiqiu was posted out as military governor of Zhenhai.

sentences.zh: 齊丘忿懟，表乞歸九華舊隱，唐主知其詐，一表，即從之，賜書曰：「今日之行，昔時相許。

translations.literal: Qiqiu, resentful and indignant, submitted a memorial begging to return to his old retreat on Mount Jiuhua. The Tang lord knew it was a feint; with a single memorial he granted it and bestowed a letter saying: "Today's departure is what was promised in former days.
translations.idiomatic: Song Qiqiu, furious, petitioned to retire to his old hermitage on Mount Jiuhua. The Tang emperor saw through the ploy; after one memorial he assented and wrote back: "The journey you take today is the one we spoke of long ago.

sentences.zh: 朕實知公，故不奪公志。」

translations.literal: I truly know you, and therefore do not deny your wish."
translations.idiomatic: I know you well, and so I will not stand in the way of your wish."

sentences.zh: 仍賜號九華先生，封青陽公，食一縣租稅。

translations.literal: He further granted him the title Master of Jiuhua, enfeoffed him as Duke of Qingyang, and assigned him the tax revenue of one county.
translations.idiomatic: He also gave him the honorific Master of Jiuhua, enfeoffed him as Duke of Qingyang, and granted him the tax revenue of one county.

sentences.zh: 齊丘乃治大第於青陽，服御將吏，皆如王公，而憤邑尤甚。

translations.literal: Qiqiu thereupon built a great mansion at Qingyang; his attendants, robes, and staff all matched those of a prince or duke, yet his resentment grew even deeper.
translations.idiomatic: Song Qiqiu then built a grand mansion at Qingyang; his household, dress, and retinue all matched princely rank, yet his bitterness only deepened.

sentences.zh: 寧州酋長莫彥殊以所部溫那等十八州附於楚；

translations.literal: The chieftain of Ning Prefecture, Mo Yanshu, submitted eighteen prefectures under his command, including Wenna, to Chu;
translations.idiomatic: Mo Yanshu, chieftain of Ningzhou, brought eighteen prefectures under his rule — including Wenna — into Chu's orbit;

sentences.zh: 其州無官府，惟立牌於岡阜，略以恩威羈縻而已。

translations.literal: those prefectures had no official administration; they merely erected placards on hilltops and loosely bound the people with a mixture of kindness and authority.
translations.idiomatic: those districts had no formal bureaucracy; placards were set up on hilltops, and the people were held in loose allegiance through a mix of favor and coercion.

sentences.zh: 是歲，春夏旱，秋冬水，蝗大起，東自海壖，西距隴坻，南逾江、湖，北抵幽薊，原野、山谷、城郭、廬舍皆滿，竹木葉俱盡。

translations.literal: That year, drought prevailed in spring and summer, floods in autumn and winter, and locusts rose in vast numbers. From the eastern seashore west to Longdi, south beyond the Yangtze and the lakes, north to You and Ji — the open fields, mountain valleys, walled cities, and dwellings were all filled; bamboo and tree leaves were entirely consumed.
translations.idiomatic: That year brought drought through spring and summer and floods through autumn and winter, and locusts swarmed in unprecedented numbers. From the eastern coast west to Longdi, south beyond the Yangtze and the great lakes, north to You and Ji — fields, valleys, cities, and homesteads were carpeted with them; every leaf on bamboo and tree was stripped bare.

sentences.zh: 重以官括民谷，使者督責嚴急，至封碓磑，不留其食，有坐匿谷抵死者。

translations.literal: Compounding this, the government requisitioned grain from the people; envoys pressed collection with harsh urgency, even sealing mills and querns and leaving them no food. Some were executed for concealing grain.
translations.idiomatic: On top of this, the government seized grain from the people. Collectors pressed their demands with brutal urgency, even sealing mills and grinding stones so that nothing was left to eat; some were put to death for hoarding grain.

sentences.zh: 縣令往往以督趣不辦，納印自劾去。

translations.literal: County magistrates often, unable to meet the urgent demands for collection, surrendered their seals and impeached themselves before departing.
translations.idiomatic: County magistrates, unable to meet the crushing collection quotas, often surrendered their seals and resigned in disgrace.

sentences.zh: 民餒死者數十萬口，流亡不可勝數。

translations.literal: Several hundred thousand people died of starvation; refugees beyond counting fled.
translations.idiomatic: Hundreds of thousands starved to death, and refugees fled in numbers beyond counting.

sentences.zh: 於是留守、節度使下至將軍，各獻馬、金、帛、芻粟以助國。

translations.literal: Thereupon, from the garrison commanders and military governors down to the generals, each presented horses, gold, silk, and fodder grain to aid the state.
translations.idiomatic: Garrison commanders, military governors, and generals alike sent horses, gold, silk, and fodder grain to aid the state.

sentences.zh: 朝廷以恆、定饑甚，獨不括民谷。

translations.literal: The court, because Heng and Ding were suffering extreme famine, alone did not requisition grain from the people.
translations.idiomatic: Because Heng and Ding were hit hardest by famine, the court alone exempted them from grain requisitions.

sentences.zh: 順國節度使杜威奏稱軍食不足，請如諸州例，許之。

translations.literal: The military governor of Shunguo, Du Wei, memorialized that military provisions were insufficient and requested to follow the example of the other prefectures; this was granted.
translations.idiomatic: Du Wei, military governor of Shunguo, reported that army rations were insufficient and asked to requisition grain like the other prefectures; the request was granted.

sentences.zh: 威用判官王緒謀，檢索殆盡，得百萬斛。

translations.literal: Wei, using the plan of his aide Wang Xu, searched and seized nearly everything, obtaining one million hu.
translations.idiomatic: Following the scheme of his aide Wang Xu, Du Wei searched the region to the last storehouse and seized one million hu of grain.

sentences.zh: 威止奏三十萬斛，餘皆入其家；

translations.literal: Wei reported only three hundred thousand hu; the remainder all went into his own household;
translations.idiomatic: He reported only three hundred thousand hu to the court; the rest went into his private coffers;

sentences.zh: 又令判官李沼稱貸於民，復滿百萬斛，來春糶之，得緡錢二百萬，闔境苦之。

translations.literal: he also had his aide Li Zhao force loans upon the people, again filling one million hu, to be sold in spring for two million strings of cash; the entire region suffered bitterly.
translations.idiomatic: he then had his aide Li Zhao extort grain loans from the people until another million hu were amassed, to be sold off the following spring for two million strings of cash — and the whole region groaned under the burden.

sentences.zh: 定州吏欲援例為奏，義武節度使馬全節不許，曰：「吾為觀察使，職在養民，豈忍效彼所為乎！」

translations.literal: Officials in Ding Prefecture wished to follow the precedent and submit a memorial; the military governor of Yiwu, Ma Quanjie, would not permit it, saying: "I serve as observation commissioner; my duty is to nourish the people — how could I bear to imitate what they did!"
translations.idiomatic: Dingzhou officials wanted to follow suit and petition for the same requisitions; Ma Quanjie, military governor of Yiwu, refused, saying: "As observation commissioner, my duty is to care for the people — how could I stoop to what they did!"

sentences.zh: 楚地多產金銀，茶利尤厚，由是財貨豐殖。

translations.literal: The lands of Chu produced much gold and silver; profits from tea were especially rich; by this the state's wealth and goods flourished.
translations.idiomatic: Chu was rich in gold and silver, and tea brought especially heavy profits; state coffers swelled accordingly.

sentences.zh: 而楚王希範，奢欲無厭，喜自誇大。

translations.literal: Yet the King of Chu, Xi Fan, was insatiable in luxury and desire and delighted in self-aggrandizement.
translations.idiomatic: Yet King Xi Fan of Chu was insatiable in his appetites and loved nothing more than glorifying himself.

sentences.zh: 為長槍大槊，飾之以金，可執而不可用。

translations.literal: He made long spears and great halberds, ornamented them with gold — fit to be held but not to be used.
translations.idiomatic: He had long spears and great halberds made, gilded for show — splendid to look at, useless in battle.

sentences.zh: 募富民年少肥澤者八千人，為銀槍都。

translations.literal: He recruited eight thousand young men from wealthy households, plump and fair-skinned, to form the Silver Spear Division.
translations.idiomatic: He recruited eight thousand young men from wealthy families — plump, fair-skinned youths — to form the Silver Spear Guard.

sentences.zh: 宮室、園囿、服用之物，務窮侈靡。

translations.literal: Palaces, gardens, and objects for daily use — all were pursued to the utmost extravagance.
translations.idiomatic: Palaces, gardens, and every object of daily use were pushed to the utmost extravagance.

sentences.zh: 作九龍殿，刻沈香為八龍，飾以金寶，長十餘丈，抱柱相向；

translations.literal: He built the Hall of Nine Dragons, carving agarwood into eight dragons and ornamenting them with gold and jewels, each more than ten zhang long, embracing pillars face to face;
translations.idiomatic: He built the Hall of Nine Dragons, carving agarwood into eight dragons studded with gold and jewels, each more than ten zhang long, coiled around pillars face to face;

sentences.zh: 希範居其中，自為一龍，其襆頭腳長丈餘，以象龍角。

translations.literal: Xi Fan dwelt among them, himself as one dragon; his official cap's flaps and feet were more than a zhang long, to resemble dragon horns.
translations.idiomatic: Xi Fan sat among them as the ninth dragon; the flaps and tails of his official cap stretched more than a zhang, fashioned to look like dragon horns.

sentences.zh: 用度不足，重為賦斂。

translations.literal: When expenditures fell short, he again imposed levies and exactions.
translations.idiomatic: When revenues ran short, he imposed fresh levies and exactions.

sentences.zh: 每遣使者行田，專以增頃畝為功，民不勝租賦而逃。

translations.literal: Whenever he sent envoys to inspect the fields, they took increasing acreage as their sole measure of merit; the people, unable to bear the rent and taxes, fled.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever he sent agents to survey the fields, success was measured only by how many acres could be added to the tax rolls; peasants, crushed by rent and levies, fled.

sentences.zh: 王曰：「但令田在，何憂無谷！」

translations.literal: The king said: "So long as the fields remain, why worry over grain!"
translations.idiomatic: The king said: "As long as the land is still there, why worry about grain!"

sentences.zh: 命營田使鄧懿文籍逃田，募民耕藝出租。

translations.literal: He ordered the commissioner of military colonies, Deng Yiwen, to register abandoned fields, recruit people to cultivate them, and collect rent.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered Deng Yiwen, commissioner of military colonies, to register abandoned fields, recruit settlers to farm them, and collect rent.

sentences.zh: 民捨故從新，僅能自存，自西徂東，各失其業。

translations.literal: The people abandoned the old for the new, barely able to survive; from west to east, each lost his former livelihood.
translations.idiomatic: People abandoned old holdings for new ones and barely scraped by; moving from west to east, each lost the livelihood he had known.

sentences.zh: 又聽人入財拜官，以財多少為官高卑之差。

translations.literal: He also permitted men to purchase office by presenting wealth, the rank granted varying in height according to the amount of wealth.
translations.idiomatic: He also allowed men to buy office with cash, rank rising or falling with the size of the payment.

sentences.zh: 富商大賈，布在列位。

translations.literal: Great merchants and rich traders were spread throughout the ranks of office.
translations.idiomatic: Wealthy merchants sat throughout the ranks of officialdom.

sentences.zh: 外官還者，必責貢獻。

translations.literal: Those returning from external posts were invariably required to present tribute.
translations.idiomatic: Officials returning from provincial posts were always required to bring tribute.

sentences.zh: 民有罪，則富者輸財，強者為兵，惟貧弱受刑。

translations.literal: When the people had crimes, the rich paid wealth, the strong became soldiers — only the poor and weak received punishment.
translations.idiomatic: When commoners were charged with crimes, the rich bought their way out with cash, the strong were pressed into service as soldiers — only the poor and weak were punished.

sentences.zh: 又置函，使人投匿名書相告訐，至有滅族者。

translations.literal: He also set up a box, allowing people to submit anonymous letters denouncing one another, until some families were exterminated to the last member.
translations.idiomatic: He also installed a denunciation box for anonymous accusations, until some families were wiped out to the last soul.

sentences.zh: 是歲，用孔目官周陟議，令常稅之外，大縣貢米二千斛，中千斛，小七百斛；

translations.literal: That year, following the proposal of the chief clerk Zhou Zhi, beyond the regular taxes, large counties were required to submit two thousand hu of rice, medium counties one thousand hu, and small counties seven hundred hu;
translations.idiomatic: That year, on the advice of chief clerk Zhou Zhi, on top of regular taxes large counties had to deliver two thousand hu of rice, medium counties one thousand, and small counties seven hundred;

sentences.zh: 無米者輸布帛。

translations.literal: those without rice submitted cloth and silk.
translations.idiomatic: counties without rice paid in cloth and silk instead.

sentences.zh: 天策學士拓跋恆上書曰：「殿下長深宮之中，藉已成之業，身不知稼穡之勞，耳不聞鼓鼙之音，馳騁遨遊，雕牆玉食。

translations.literal: The Tianji Academician Tuoba Heng submitted a memorial saying: "Your Highness has long dwelt deep within the palace, relying on an already established enterprise. You do not know the toil of sowing and reaping with your own body, nor do your ears hear the sound of drums and war-horns. You gallop and roam in pleasure, with carved walls and jade fare.
translations.idiomatic: Tianji Academician Tuoba Heng submitted a memorial: "Your Highness has long lived deep in the palace, resting on an inheritance already won. You have never felt the labor of the fields, never heard the drums of war. You ride and hunt for pleasure, dine off jade, and dwell within carved walls.

sentences.zh: 府庫盡矣，而浮費益甚；

translations.literal: The treasury is exhausted, yet wasteful spending grows ever greater;
translations.idiomatic: The treasury is empty, yet wasteful spending grows ever greater;

sentences.zh: 百姓困矣，而厚斂不息。

translations.literal: the people are distressed, yet heavy exactions do not cease.
translations.idiomatic: the people are in misery, yet heavy exactions never stop.

sentences.zh: 今淮南為仇讎之國，番禺懷吞噬之志，荊渚日圖窺伺，溪洞待我姑息。

translations.literal: Now Huainan is a nation of sworn enemies; Panyu harbors designs of swallowing us; Jingzhu daily plots to watch for openings; the stream-cave peoples wait upon our indulgence.
translations.idiomatic: Huainan is a sworn enemy; Panyu hungers to swallow us; Jingzhou watches daily for weakness; the hill tribes wait on our forbearance.

sentences.zh: 諺曰：『足寒傷心，民怨傷國。』

translations.literal: A proverb says: 'When the feet are cold, the heart is injured; when the people resent, the state is injured.'
translations.idiomatic: A proverb says: 'Cold feet chill the heart; popular resentment wounds the state.'

sentences.zh: 願罷輸米之令，誅周陟以謝郡縣，去不急之務，減興作之役。

translations.literal: I beg that the order to submit rice be abolished, that Zhou Zhi be executed to appease the commanderies and counties, that unurgent affairs be set aside, and that construction and corvée labor be reduced.
translations.idiomatic: I beg you to revoke the rice tribute, execute Zhou Zhi to answer the provinces and counties, drop unurgent business, and cut construction and corvée.

sentences.zh: 無令一旦禍敗，為四方所笑。」

translations.literal: Do not let disaster and ruin come in a single day, to be laughed at by all quarters."
translations.idiomatic: Do not invite sudden ruin and become a laughingstock to every quarter."

sentences.zh: 王大怒。

translations.literal: The king was greatly enraged.
translations.idiomatic: The king flew into a rage.

sentences.zh: 他日，恆請見，辭以晝寢。

translations.literal: On another day, when Heng requested an audience, the king declined on the grounds that he was napping at midday.
translations.idiomatic: Another day, when Heng asked for an audience, the king refused, pleading a midday nap.

sentences.zh: 恆謂客將區弘練曰：「王逞欲而愎諫，吾見其千口飄零無日矣。」

translations.literal: Heng said to the guest officer Qu Honglian: "The king indulges his desires and rejects remonstrance; I see that the day is not far when his thousand mouths will scatter and fall."
translations.idiomatic: Heng told guest officer Qu Honglian: "The king follows his appetites and spurns honest counsel; I see the day coming when his whole clan will be scattered to the winds."

sentences.zh: 王益怒，遂終身不復見之。

translations.literal: The king grew still angrier and from then on never received him again for the rest of his life.
translations.idiomatic: The king's rage only deepened, and he never granted Heng an audience again for the rest of his life.

sentences.zh: 閩主曦嫁其女，取班簿閱視之；

translations.literal: The Lord of Min, Xi, gave his daughter in marriage and took out the roster of officials to review it;
translations.idiomatic: When Lord Xi of Min gave his daughter in marriage, he took out the roster of officials to review it;

sentences.zh: 朝士有不賀者十二人，皆杖之於朝堂。

translations.literal: twelve court officials who had not offered congratulations were all beaten in the audience hall.
translations.idiomatic: twelve court officials who had failed to offer congratulations were flogged in the audience hall.

sentences.zh: 以御史中丞劉贊不舉劾，亦將杖之，贊義不受辱，欲自殺。

translations.literal: Because the censor-in-chief Liu Zan had not impeached them, he too was about to be beaten; Zan, holding that he ought not suffer such disgrace, wished to kill himself.
translations.idiomatic: Because Censor-in-Chief Liu Zan had not impeached them, he too was to be flogged; Liu Zan, unwilling to endure such humiliation, tried to take his own life.

sentences.zh: 諫議大夫鄭元弼諫曰：「古者刑不上大夫，中丞儀刑百僚，豈宜加之棰楚！」

translations.literal: The Remonstrance Officer Zheng Yuanbi remonstrated, saying: "In antiquity, punishment did not reach the grandees; the censor-in-chief is the model of discipline for the hundred officials — how can the rod and whip be applied to him!"
translations.idiomatic: Remonstrance Officer Zheng Yuanbi protested: "In antiquity, punishment did not reach high officials; the censor-in-chief sets the standard for all the bureaucracy — how can he be beaten with rod and whip!"

sentences.zh: 曦正色曰：「卿欲效魏徵邪？」

translations.literal: Xi, with a stern countenance, said: "Do you wish to imitate Wei Zheng?"
translations.idiomatic: Xi said sternly: "Do you mean to play Wei Zheng to me?"

sentences.zh: 元弼曰：「臣以陛下為唐太宗，故敢效魏徵。」

translations.literal: Yuanbi said: "I take Your Majesty to be Emperor Taizong of Tang, and therefore dare to imitate Wei Zheng."
translations.idiomatic: Yuanbi replied: "Because I take Your Majesty for Emperor Taizong of Tang, I dare play Wei Zheng."

sentences.zh: 曦怒稍解，乃釋贊，贊竟以憂卒。

translations.literal: Xi's anger eased somewhat; he thereupon released Zan, but Zan ultimately died of grief.
translations.idiomatic: Xi's anger subsided somewhat; he released Liu Zan, but Liu Zan died of grief all the same.

sentences.zh: 高祖聖文章武明德孝皇帝下開運元年（

translations.literal: Emperor Gaozu, the Sage, Cultured, Martial, Brightly Virtuous, and Filially Reverent — Lower [Section], First Year of Kaiyun (
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Gaozu the Sage, Cultured, Martial, Brightly Virtuous, and Filially Reverent — Lower Section, First Year of Kaiyun (

sentences.zh: 甲辰，公元九四四年）

translations.literal: jiachen, CE 944)
translations.idiomatic: jiachen, 944 CE)

sentences.zh: 春，正月，乙亥，邊籓馳告：「契丹前鋒將趙延壽、趙延照將兵五萬入寇，逼貝州。」

translations.literal: In spring, the first month, on yihai, the border garrisons sent urgent reports: "The Khitan vanguard generals Zhao Yanshou and Zhao Yanzhao are leading fifty thousand troops in invasion, pressing upon Bei Prefecture."
translations.idiomatic: In spring, the first month, on yihai, frontier garrisons sent urgent word: "Khitan vanguard generals Zhao Yanshou and Zhao Yanzhao are leading fifty thousand men in invasion, closing on Beizhou."

sentences.zh: 延照，思溫之子也。

translations.literal: Yanzhao was the son of Siwen.
translations.idiomatic: Yanzhao was the son of Siwen.

sentences.zh: 先是朝廷以貝州水陸要衝，多聚芻粟，為大軍數年之儲，以備契丹。

translations.literal: Earlier, the court, because Bei Prefecture was a strategic junction by land and water, had gathered much fodder and grain there as several years' stores for a great army, to guard against the Khitan.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, because Beizhou was a strategic crossroads by land and water, the court had stockpiled fodder and grain there — enough for a great army to live on for years — against a Khitan attack.

sentences.zh: 軍校邵珂，性凶悖，永清節度使王令溫黜之。

translations.literal: The army officer Shao Ke was by nature fierce and rebellious; the military governor of Yongqing, Wang Lingwen, dismissed him.
translations.idiomatic: Army officer Shao Ke was violent and insubordinate; Wang Lingwen, military governor of Yongqing, removed him from his post.

sentences.zh: 珂怨望，密遣人亡入契丹，言「貝州粟多而兵弱，易取也。」

translations.literal: Ke, resentful, secretly sent men to slip into the Khitan camp and say: "Bei Prefecture has much grain but weak troops — it is easy to take."
translations.idiomatic: Shao Ke, nursing a grudge, secretly sent men into the Khitan camp with word that Beizhou was rich in grain but weak in troops — an easy prize."

sentences.zh: 會令溫入朝，執政以前復州防禦使吳巒權知州事。

translations.literal: It happened that Lingwen went to court; the chief ministers appointed the former defense commissioner of Fuzhou, Wu Luan, to serve temporarily as prefect.
translations.idiomatic: Just then Wang Lingwen went to court; the chief ministers appointed former Fuzhou defense commissioner Wu Luan acting prefect.

sentences.zh: 巒至，推誠撫士；

translations.literal: When Luan arrived, he treated the soldiers with sincerity and kindness;
translations.idiomatic: When Wu Luan arrived, he treated the troops with open sincerity;

sentences.zh: 會契丹入寇，巒書生，無爪牙，珂自請，願效死，巒使將兵守南門，巒自守東門。

translations.literal: when the Khitan invasion came, Luan was a scholar and had no strong arms; Ke volunteered, saying he wished to die in service. Luan had him lead troops to hold the south gate; Luan himself held the east gate.
translations.idiomatic: when the Khitan invasion came, Wu Luan was a scholar with no hardened fighters of his own; Shao Ke volunteered to die in the city's defense. Wu Luan put him in charge of the south gate and held the east gate himself.

sentences.zh: 契丹主自攻貝州，巒悉力拒之，燒其攻具殆盡。

translations.literal: The Khitan ruler himself attacked Bei Prefecture; Luan resisted with all his strength and burned their siege engines nearly to destruction.
translations.idiomatic: The Khitan khagan himself besieged Beizhou; Wu Luan resisted with everything he had and burned the siege engines nearly to ashes.

sentences.zh: 己卯，契丹復攻城，珂引契丹自南門入，巒赴井死。

translations.literal: On jimao, the Khitan again assaulted the city; Ke led the Khitan in through the south gate, and Luan threw himself into a well and died.
translations.idiomatic: On jimao the Khitan assaulted the city again; Shao Ke opened the south gate and let them in. Wu Luan threw himself into a well and died.

sentences.zh: 契丹遂陷貝州，所殺且萬人。

translations.literal: The Khitan thereupon captured Bei Prefecture; those killed numbered nearly ten thousand.
translations.idiomatic: The Khitan then took Beizhou; nearly ten thousand were slaughtered.

sentences.zh: 庚辰，以歸德節度使高行周為北面行營都部署，以河陽節度使符彥卿為馬軍左廂排陳使，以右神武統軍皇甫遇為馬軍右廂排陳使，以陝府節度使王周為步軍左廂排陳使，以左羽林將軍潘環為步軍右廂排陳使。

translations.literal: On gengchen, the military governor of Guide, Gao Xingzhou, was appointed overall commander of the northern campaign; the military governor of Heyang, Fu Yanqing, was made left wing commander of the cavalry; the commander-in-chief of the Right Divine Martial Army, Huangfu Yu, was made right wing commander of the cavalry; the military governor of Shan Prefecture, Wang Zhou, was made left wing commander of the infantry; and the Left Feathered Forest General Pan Huan was made right wing commander of the infantry.
translations.idiomatic: On gengchen, Gao Xingzhou, military governor of Guide, was named overall commander of the northern campaign; Fu Yanqing of Heyang was made left cavalry wing commander; Huangfu Yu, commander-in-chief of the Right Divine Martial Army, right cavalry wing commander; Wang Zhou of Shanzhou, left infantry wing commander; and Left Feathered Forest General Pan Huan, right infantry wing commander.

sentences.zh: 太原奏契丹入雁門關。

translations.literal: Taiyuan reported that the Khitan had entered Yanmen Pass.
translations.idiomatic: Taiyuan reported that the Khitan had crossed Yanmen Pass.

sentences.zh: 恆、邢、滄皆奏契丹入寇。

translations.literal: Heng, Xing, and Cang all reported Khitan invasion.
translations.idiomatic: Heng, Xing, and Cang all reported Khitan incursions.

sentences.zh: 成德節度使杜威遣幕僚曹光裔詣楊光遠，為陳禍福，光遠遣光裔入奏，稱：「承祚逃歸，母疾故爾。

translations.literal: The military governor of Chengde, Du Wei, sent his staff officer Cao Guangyi to Yang Guangyuan to set forth fortune and disaster; Guangyuan sent Guangyi to court to report, saying: "Chengzuo fled back because his mother was ill.
translations.idiomatic: Du Wei, military governor of Chengde, sent staff officer Cao Guangyi to Yang Guangyuan to argue the costs of rebellion; Guangyuan sent Cao to court with word that Chengzuo had fled home because his mother was ill.

sentences.zh: 既蒙恩宥，闔族荷恩。」

translations.literal: Having received the court's gracious pardon, the whole clan bears gratitude."
translations.idiomatic: Having received the court's gracious pardon, our whole clan is bound in gratitude."

sentences.zh: 朝廷信其言，遣使與光裔復往慰諭之。

translations.literal: The court believed his words and dispatched an envoy with Guangyi to go again and reassure him.
translations.idiomatic: The court believed him and sent an envoy with Cao Guangyi back to reassure him.

sentences.zh: 唐以侍中周宗為鎮南節度使，左僕射兼門下侍郎、同平章事張居詠為鎮海節度使。

translations.literal: Tang appointed Vice Grand Councilor Zhou Zong military governor of Zhennan and Left Vice Director of the Secretariat, Left Minister of Works, and Co-Equal to the Three Excellencies Zhang Juyong military governor of Zhenhai.
translations.idiomatic: Tang appointed Vice Grand Councilor Zhou Zong military governor of Zhennan and Left Vice Director of the Secretariat, Left Minister of Works, and Co-Equal to the Three Excellencies Zhang Juyong military governor of Zhenhai.

sentences.zh: 唐主決欲傳位於齊、燕二王。

translations.literal: The Tang lord was firmly resolved to transmit the throne to the Princes of Qi and Yan.
translations.idiomatic: The Tang emperor was firmly resolved to pass the throne to the Princes of Qi and Yan.

sentences.zh: 翰林學士馮延己等因之欲隔絕中外以擅權。

translations.literal: The Hanlin Academician Feng Yanji and others, taking advantage of this, wished to cut off contact between inside and outside so as to monopolize power.
translations.idiomatic: Hanlin Academician Feng Yanji and his circle seized on the moment, hoping to cut the court off from the outside world and keep power in their own hands.

sentences.zh: 辛巳，敕：「齊王景遂參決庶政，百官惟樞密副使魏岑、查文徽得白事，餘非召對不得見。」

translations.literal: On xinsi, an edict stated: "Prince Jing of Qi shall participate in deciding ordinary affairs of government; among the hundred officials, only the deputy commissioners of the Bureau of Military Affairs, Wei Cen and Zha Wenhui, may report matters directly; the rest may not be received unless summoned."
