translations.idiomatic: On xinsi an edict declared: "Prince Jing of Qi shall share in deciding routine government; of all officials, only Deputy Commissioners of Military Affairs Wei Cen and Zha Wenhui may report business directly — the rest may not be received unless summoned."

sentences.zh: 國人大駭。

translations.literal: The people of the state were greatly alarmed.
translations.idiomatic: The realm was shaken.

sentences.zh: 給事中蕭儼上疏極論，不報。

translations.literal: The Supervising Secretary Xiao Yan submitted a memorial arguing to the utmost; no reply was given.
translations.idiomatic: Supervising Secretary Xiao Yan submitted a fierce memorial of protest; no answer came.

sentences.zh: 侍衛都虞候賈崇叩閣求見，曰：「臣事先帝三十年，觀其延接疏遠，孜孜不怠，下情猶有不通者。

translations.literal: The Chief of Palace Guards Jia Chong knocked at the gate and requested an audience, saying: "I served the late emperor for thirty years and observed how he received those near and far, diligent and untiring; yet even so, the feelings of those below were sometimes not fully conveyed.
translations.idiomatic: Chief of Palace Guards Jia Chong knocked at the palace gate and begged an audience: "I served the late emperor for thirty years and watched him receive men high and low with tireless diligence — yet even then the voices below did not always reach him.

sentences.zh: 陛下新即位，所任者何人，而頓與群臣謝絕？

translations.literal: Your Majesty has newly ascended the throne — whom do you appoint, that you suddenly cut yourself off from the whole body of ministers?
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty has only just taken the throne — whom have you put in charge, that you suddenly shut the ministers out entirely?

sentences.zh: 臣老矣，不復得奉顏色。」

translations.literal: I am old and shall no longer be able to behold your countenance."
translations.idiomatic: I am old; I shall never again look upon your face."

sentences.zh: 因涕泗嗚咽。

translations.literal: He thereupon wept and sobbed aloud.
translations.idiomatic: He broke down in tears.

sentences.zh: 唐主感悟，遽收前敕。

translations.literal: The Tang lord was moved to understanding and immediately withdrew the earlier edict.
translations.idiomatic: The Tang emperor was moved and at once revoked the edict.

sentences.zh: 唐主於宮中作高樓，召侍臣觀之，眾皆歎美。

translations.literal: The Tang lord built a high tower within the palace and summoned the attendant ministers to view it; all sighed in admiration.
translations.idiomatic: The Tang emperor built a high tower in the palace and summoned his ministers to view it; all murmured in admiration.

sentences.zh: 蕭儼曰：「恨樓下無井。」

translations.literal: Xiao Yan said: "I only regret that there is no well beneath the tower."
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Yan said: "My only regret is that there is no well beneath the tower."

sentences.zh: 唐主問其故。

translations.literal: The Tang lord asked the reason.
translations.idiomatic: The Tang emperor asked why.

sentences.zh: 對曰：「以此不及景陽樓耳。」

translations.literal: He replied: "Because of this it does not reach the Jingyang Tower, that is all."
translations.idiomatic: He answered, "That's why it falls short of the Jingyang Tower."

sentences.zh: 唐主怒，貶於舒州，觀察使孫晟遣兵防之，儼曰：「儼以諫諍得罪，非有它志。

translations.literal: The Tang ruler was enraged and demoted him to Shuzhou. Observation Commissioner Sun Sheng dispatched troops to guard him. Yan said: "Yan was punished for remonstrating and offering counsel; I have no other intent.
translations.idiomatic: The Tang ruler flew into a rage and banished him to Shuzhou. Observation Commissioner Sun Sheng sent troops to keep watch over him. Yan declared, "I was punished only for speaking out in remonstrance—I have no other designs.

sentences.zh: 昔顧命之際，君幾危社稷，其罪顧不重於儼乎？

translations.literal: At the time of the entrusted final charge, you nearly endangered the altars of state—was your offense not clearly heavier than Yan's?
translations.idiomatic: When you received the dying sovereign's charge, you nearly brought the realm to ruin. Surely your guilt outweighs mine?

sentences.zh: 今日反見防邪！」

translations.literal: Yet today I am placed under guard instead!"
translations.idiomatic: And now I am the one placed under guard?"

sentences.zh: 晟慚懼，遽罷之。

translations.literal: Sheng, ashamed and afraid, immediately dismissed the guard.
translations.idiomatic: Ashamed and alarmed, Sun Sheng at once withdrew the guard.

sentences.zh: 帝遣使持書遺契丹，契丹已屯鄴都，不得通而返。

translations.literal: The Emperor sent an envoy bearing a letter to the Khitan. The Khitan had already encamped at Yedu and could not be reached, so he returned.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor sent an envoy with a letter to the Khitan, but the Khitan had already encamped at Yedu; unable to get through, the envoy turned back.

sentences.zh: 壬午，以侍衛馬步都指揮使景延廣為御營使，前靖難節度使李周為東京留守。

translations.literal: On renwu, Jing Yanguang, commander-in-chief of the palace cavalry and infantry, was made commander of the imperial camp; the former Jingnan military governor Li Zhou was made governor of the Eastern Capital.
translations.idiomatic: On renwu, Jing Yanguang, commander-in-chief of the palace cavalry and infantry, was appointed commander of the imperial camp, and the former Jingnan military governor Li Zhou was made governor of the Eastern Capital.

sentences.zh: 是日，高行周以前軍先發。

translations.literal: That day, Gao Xingzhou led the vanguard in departing first.
translations.idiomatic: That same day Gao Xingzhou marched out first at the head of the vanguard.

sentences.zh: 時用兵方略號令皆出延廣，宰相以下皆無所預；

translations.literal: At the time all military strategy and orders issued from Yanguang; from the chief ministers downward none had any part in them;
translations.idiomatic: At the time all strategy and commands came from Yanguang alone; the chief ministers and everyone below had no say in them;

sentences.zh: 延廣乘勢使氣，陵侮諸將，雖天子亦不能制。

translations.literal: Yanguang, riding his power and venting his temper, insulted and humiliated the generals—even the Son of Heaven could not restrain him.
translations.idiomatic: Yanguang, swollen with power and arrogance, bullied and humiliated the generals; not even the Emperor could check him.

sentences.zh: 乙酉，帝發東京。

translations.literal: On yiyou, the Emperor departed the Eastern Capital.
translations.idiomatic: On yiyou the Emperor set out from the Eastern Capital.

sentences.zh: 丁亥，滑州奏契丹至黎陽。

translations.literal: On dinghai, Hua Prefecture reported that the Khitan had reached Liyang.
translations.idiomatic: On dinghai Hua Prefecture reported that the Khitan had reached Liyang.

sentences.zh: 戊子，帝至澶州。

translations.literal: On wuzi, the Emperor reached Cazhou.
translations.idiomatic: On wuzi the Emperor arrived at Cazhou.

sentences.zh: 契丹主屯元城，趙延壽屯南樂；

translations.literal: The Khitan ruler encamped at Yuancheng; Zhao Yanshou encamped at Nanle;
translations.idiomatic: The Khitan ruler encamped at Yuancheng, and Zhao Yanshou encamped at Nanle;

sentences.zh: 以延壽為魏博節度使，封魏王。

translations.literal: Yanshou was made military governor of Weibo and enfeoffed as Prince of Wei.
translations.idiomatic: Yanshou was appointed military governor of Weibo and enfeoffed as Prince of Wei.

sentences.zh: 契丹寇太原，劉知遠與白承福合兵二萬擊之。

translations.literal: The Khitan raided Taiyuan; Liu Zhiyuan and Bai Chengfu combined forces of twenty thousand to strike them.
translations.idiomatic: The Khitan attacked Taiyuan; Liu Zhiyuan and Bai Chengfu joined forces—twenty thousand men—and struck back.

sentences.zh: 甲午，以知遠為幽州道行營招討使，杜威為副使，馬全節為都虞候。

translations.literal: On jiawu, Liu Zhiyuan was made campaign commander for the Youzhou circuit; Du Wei was deputy commander; Ma Quanjie was chief adjutant.
translations.idiomatic: On jiawu Liu Zhiyuan was made campaign commander on the Youzhou route, with Du Wei as deputy and Ma Quanjie as chief adjutant.

sentences.zh: 丙申，遣右武衛上將軍張彥澤等將兵拒契丹於黎陽。

translations.literal: On bingshen, Right Martial Guard senior general Zhang Yanze and others were dispatched to lead troops and resist the Khitan at Liyang.
translations.idiomatic: On bingshen Zhang Yanze, senior general of the Right Martial Guard, and others were sent to lead troops against the Khitan at Liyang.

sentences.zh: 戊戌，蜀主復以將相遙領節度使。

translations.literal: On wuxu, the Shu ruler again had generals and ministers hold military governorships in absentia.
translations.idiomatic: On wuxu the Shu ruler again had his generals and ministers hold military governorships in absentia.

sentences.zh: 帝復遣譯者孟守忠致書於契丹，求修舊好。

translations.literal: The Emperor again sent the interpreter Meng Shouzhong to deliver a letter to the Khitan, seeking to restore the former friendship.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor again sent the interpreter Meng Shouzhong with a letter to the Khitan, asking to renew the old alliance.

sentences.zh: 契丹主復書曰：「已成之勢，不可改也。」

translations.literal: The Khitan ruler replied in writing: "The situation already established cannot be changed."
translations.idiomatic: The Khitan ruler wrote back: "What is already settled cannot be undone."

sentences.zh: 辛丑，太原奏破契丹偉王於秀容，斬首三千級。

translations.literal: On xinchou, Taiyuan reported defeating the Khitan Prince Wei at Xiurong, beheading three thousand.
translations.idiomatic: On xinchou Taiyuan reported a victory over the Khitan Prince Wei at Xiurong, with three thousand heads taken.

sentences.zh: 契丹自鴉鳴谷遁去。

translations.literal: The Khitan fled through Yamming Gorge.
translations.idiomatic: The Khitan withdrew through Yamming Gorge.

sentences.zh: 殷鑄天德通寶大鐵錢，一當百。

translations.literal: Yin cast large iron coins of the Tiande Tongbao, each worth a hundred.
translations.idiomatic: Yin cast large iron Tiande Tongbao coins, each valued at a hundred standard coins.

sentences.zh: 唐主遣使遺閩主曦及殷主延政書，責以兄弟尋戈。

translations.literal: The Tang ruler sent envoys delivering letters to the Min ruler Xi and the Yin ruler Yanzheng, reproaching them for brothers taking up arms against one another.
translations.idiomatic: The Tang ruler sent envoys with letters to the Min ruler Xi and the Yin ruler Yanzheng, rebuking them for fratricidal war.

sentences.zh: 曦復書，引周公誅管、蔡，唐太宗誅建成、元吉為比。

translations.literal: Xi replied in writing, citing as parallels the Duke of Zhou's execution of Guan and Cai, and Emperor Taizong of Tang's execution of Jiancheng and Yuanji.
translations.idiomatic: Xi wrote back, comparing himself to the Duke of Zhou's punishment of Guan and Cai and to Emperor Taizong's execution of Jiancheng and Yuanji.

sentences.zh: 延政復書，斥唐主奪楊氏國。

translations.literal: Yanzheng replied in writing, denouncing the Tang ruler for seizing the Yang clan's realm.
translations.idiomatic: Yanzheng wrote back, accusing the Tang ruler of usurping the Yang family's kingdom.

sentences.zh: 唐主怒，遂與殷絕。

translations.literal: The Tang ruler was enraged and thereupon broke with Yin.
translations.idiomatic: The Tang ruler was furious and broke off relations with Yin.

sentences.zh: 天平節度副使、知鄆州顏衎遣觀察判官竇儀奏：「博州刺史周儒以城降契丹，又與楊光遠通使往還，引契丹自馬家口濟河，擒左武衛將軍蔡行遇。」

translations.literal: Yan Kan, deputy military governor of Tianping and acting prefect of Yanzhou, sent Observation Corps judge Dou Yi to memorialize: "Bo Prefecture governor Zhou Ru surrendered the city to the Khitan, and also exchanged envoys back and forth with Yang Guangyuan, guiding the Khitan to cross the river at Majiakou and capturing Left Martial Guard General Cai Xingyu."
translations.idiomatic: Yan Kan, deputy military governor of Tianping and acting prefect of Yanzhou, had Observation Corps judge Dou Yi submit a memorial: "Bo Prefecture governor Zhou Ru surrendered his city to the Khitan, exchanged envoys with Yang Guangyuan, and guided the Khitan across the river at Majiakou, where they captured Left Martial Guard General Cai Xingyu."

sentences.zh: 儀謂景延廣曰：「虜若濟河與光遠合，則河南危矣。」

translations.literal: Yi said to Jing Yanguang: "If the barbarians cross the river and join with Guangyuan, then the region south of the Yellow River will be in peril."
translations.idiomatic: Yi told Jing Yanguang, "If the enemy crosses the river and links up with Guangyuan, the lands south of the Yellow River will be in grave danger."

sentences.zh: 延廣然之。

translations.literal: Yanguang agreed with this.
translations.idiomatic: Yanguang agreed.

sentences.zh: 儀，薊州人也。

translations.literal: Yi was a native of Jizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Yi was from Jizhou.
